* Students: Accepted.

* Sheikh: Accepted. And because the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are the clearest and most explicit of speech, it is not possible for them to contain any complexity, neither verbal nor conceptual. Rather, it is clear and manifest in its meaning. And because the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are the most truthful of speech, it is not possible for Him, the Mighty and Majestic, to inform us of a matter that did not happen, or of a matter whose reality is contrary to it. And because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the most desirous of making things clear, meaning He loves to make things clear to His servants more than anyone. Recite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [an-Nisa' 176], and similar verses indicating that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wishes to make clear to His servants what they may be guided by. So if He, glorified and exalted, is the most desirous of speaking clearly, or He is the most beloved of those to whom clarity is directed, that being Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then Allah, exalted is He, cannot say in His speech anything in which there is no clarity for us.

So we deny them and we say: You have lied that the alternation of night and day is due to the earth's rotation. Rather, the alternation of night and day is due to the sun's rotation around the earth, and there is nothing strange in that.

They say: How can the large revolve around the small?

We say: There is no objection. We agree with you that the sun is larger than the earth, but what prevents the larger part, or the larger body, from revolving around the smaller?

When we look at the Qur'an, we find that Allah, glorified and exalted, attributes this movement to the sun itself. Likewise, when we look at the Sunnah. In the Qur'an Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you see the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. And in the Qur'an Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, I preferred the love of good [wealth] over the remembrance of my Lord until it was hidden behind the veil﴾ [Sad 32], meaning: the sun ﴿behind the veil﴾. And in the Qur'an He says: ﴿He subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term﴾ [Luqman 29]. These are six places.

* Student: ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place﴾.

* Sheikh: ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place﴾ [Ya-Sin 38], like ﴿each runs to a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13]. All of them indicate that these actions occur from the sun. If this were due to the earth's rotation, it would say: "And you see the sun when they rise upon it", because the earth turned and so we are the ones who rise upon the sun, and it is not the sun that rises upon us.

As for their claim that this is an address to people about what they see with their eyes, and the matter is the opposite: that is, when it rises according to what the eye sees.

In reality, it is we who rise upon it. So how do we respond to them?

We say: This contradicts Allah's command, and we cannot turn away from this apparent meaning except by a sensory proof, which we can present before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because Allah will call us to account, saying: Why did you turn away from My words to the words of others? The address is from Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿when it rises, inclining away from their cave﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. ﴿Inclining﴾ means it bends. If this were due to the earth's rotation, then it would be the earth that inclines. ﴿And when it sets﴾: if this were due to the earth's rotation, it would be the earth that sets away from the sun.

As for the Sunnah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr when the sun set: "Do you know where it goes?" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3199) and Muslim (159 / 250) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] "Do you know where it goes?" He attributed the going to it when it set. If it were the earth that turned until the sun disappeared, he would have said: "Do you know where the earth goes, for example?"

In summary: it is obligatory upon us to hold to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, that the sun is what revolves around the earth, and that by its revolution the alternation of night and day occurs. This is the obligation, and it is not permissible to turn away from this at all, except when a sensory proof establishes otherwise, in which case interpretation (ta'wil) and redirecting the words from their apparent meaning become necessary. This is because we know with certainty that the Qur'an does not contradict reality. As for something they say by their assumptions and estimations, we do not agree with them on it, and it is not fitting for a believer to turn away from the apparent meaning of Allah's words merely because of their saying, never.

As for the question of whether the earth revolves or does not revolve, we say: we neither affirm nor deny it. It is possible that it has a revolution, and nevertheless the sun has a revolution.

They say: If you affirm the earth's revolution, it necessarily follows that you must say the sun is stationary. We say: That does not necessarily follow. It is possible that the sun has a revolution and the earth has another revolution, and there is no objection to that. But nevertheless we say: discussing the earth's revolution is among the superfluous knowledge that a person should not waste his time on, except for someone who needs to know it, as it is said they need it for guided missiles and similar things known to its specialists. In that case, if he needs it, there is no harm in his researching it. But if he does not need it, we say: this is a waste of time. What is the benefit of knowing whether it revolves or does not revolve? Praise Allah that He made it a resting place, whether it revolves or does not.

He said: ﴿Each runs to a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13]. The particle lam may be for purpose (al-'āqibah): that is, each runs until it reaches this term. And it may be that the lam means "to" (ilā), as it came in another place: ﴿Each runs to a specified term﴾ [Luqman 29].

In any case, it indicates that this running has an end, and so it is. This end was explained by the author with his words: "the Day of Resurrection."

His words: ﴿a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13] mean determined, known to whom? To Allah, glorified and exalted. It is known to Him and not known to us.

So these sun and moon are not eternal, but they are continuous, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant﴾ [Ibrahim 33], meaning continuing; but they have a term: ﴿Each runs to a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]. The demonstrative refers to what was mentioned of the subjection and the running. Pay attention! I say: ﴿That﴾ refers to what was mentioned of the subjection and running, or does it refer to the agent in His words ﴿subjected﴾?

* Student: The agent.

* Sheikh: So: that Subjecter is Allah. The one pointed to now is singular masculine, and the addressees are a plural of males.

Here we ask: what is taken into account with the demonstrative noun and the second-person suffix kaf? Is the addressee taken into account or the one being pointed to?

We say: as for the demonstrative noun, what is taken into account is the one pointed to. As for the kaf, what is taken into account is the addressee. Do you understand? So if you point to two men while addressing a group of females, or point to two males while addressing a group of females, what do you say?

* Student: Hadhan.

* Sheikh: No.

* Student: Dhānikunna.

* Sheikh: We say: dhānikunna. (dhānī) addresses two males, (kunna) addresses a group of females: dhānikunna. In the Qur'an: ﴿She said: That is the one you blamed me for﴾ [Yusuf 32], but here in the verse the one pointed to is singular masculine. The one pointed to is singular masculine.

[Addressing a group of males while pointing to a group of females.]

* Student: Ulā'ikum.

* Another student: Tilkum.

* Sheikh: Tilkum, correct? Tilkum or ulā'ikum? Both are acceptable.

Is the most eloquent form for the addressee that the pronoun follows the addressee: a plural of males if the addressee is a plural of males, a plural of females if the addressee is a plural of females, a dual if the addressee is a dual, a singular with a fatha if the addressee is masculine, a singular with a kasra if the addressee is feminine? Or is the most eloquent form always the singular?

We say: there are three dialects:

First: that it follows the addressee absolutely. This is one.

Second: that it is always with a fatha, meaning for the singular: with a fatha for the singular.

Third: that it is with a fatha for the singular in the masculine, and with a kasra in the feminine absolutely. How many are these? Three dialects. Do you conceive them well, or not?

* Students: Yes.

* Sheikh: The first dialect, which is the famous and eloquent one: that the kaf follows the addressee absolutely. You address a singular masculine and say (dhālika), a singular feminine (dhālika with a kasra: dhālika), a dual (dhālikumā), a plural of males (dhālikum), a plural of females (dhālikunna). This is the most eloquent.

Second: that you make it a singular with a fatha in the masculine absolutely, so you say (dhālika), whether you are addressing a singular, a dual, or a plural, but on condition that it is masculine.

And you say in the feminine: (dhālikī), whether you are addressing one woman, a group, or two.

Third: that you make it with a fatha in the form of the masculine always, whoever you address. So you say (dhālika), whether you are addressing a man or a woman, a group, a dual, or a singular.

Here Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13]. The one pointed to in the verse, ﴿That﴾: what is its type?

* Students: Dual.

* Sheikh: No. The one pointed to is singular masculine, and the addressee is a group, because Allah addresses all of mankind.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13]. The Lord (al-Rabb) is used in the Arabic language for many meanings:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 13–14 (part 2 of 3):

Among them: the Creator, the Owner, the Governor. Lordship (rububiyyah) means that Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Creator, the Owner, and the Governor. For this reason He said: ﴿To Him belongs dominion﴾. This is a declarative sentence in which the predicate has been placed first to indicate restriction (hasr). The meaning is: dominion belongs to Him alone, to the exclusion of anyone else. It is absolute dominion, encompassing Allah alone: dominion over essences and substances, and dominion over the disposal of these substances. He is the Owner of every creature, and He is the one who disposes of every creature.

If you say: How is the restriction valid, given that Allah Almighty has affirmed ownership for others, when He said: ﴿except over their spouses or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 6], and He said: ﴿or what you possess the keys to﴾ [al-Nur 61], and He said: ﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission from among those whom your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur 33]? He has affirmed ownership for others. How, then, can you say that this sentence contains restriction?

The answer has two aspects.

The first aspect: our ownership is not absolute ownership; rather, it is ownership restricted by the Shari'ah. For example, I own this bag, but I do not have the right to destroy it. Do I have the right to destroy it? Never, because it is forbidden for me to destroy it. I own this camel, for example, but do I have the right to torture it? Do I have the right to wound it? By Allah, I would love to wound this camel, but I do not have this right except by permission from the Shari'ah. For this reason, when the Shari'ah permitted branding, branding the camel, although it is harmful and painful to it, it was permitted. And when it permitted ish'ar (marking) of camels and cattle in the sacrificial offering (hady), it was permitted.

Do you know ish'ar? Ish'ar is to cut the hump with a knife in the sacrificial animal until the blood flows over the hair and the skin. What is the benefit of this?

The benefit is so that it is known that this is a hady. For this reason we do ish'ar to camels and cattle, and we garland (taqlid) camels, cattle and sheep.

Sheep are not marked; they are only garlanded.

It seems the brother says: What is taqlid? Taqlid means that we place a garland around the neck, and we hang on it old, torn sandals and the ears of waterskins (qirab). Waterskins are known; the singular of qirab is qirbah. The ears of waterskins, meaning pieces of waterskins, are attached to it. We hang this on the camel, cow or sheep. Why? So that it is known that it is a hady, because torn sandals and pieces of waterskins indicate shabbiness and poverty, a sign that this is for the poor. But our point, returning to the original matter: is our ownership of the thing restricted or absolute?

* Students: Restricted.
* The Shaykh: Restricted, yes indeed.

The second aspect: it is an inferior (qasir) ownership, meaning it is not comprehensive. For example, I own this bag, but you do not own it, and you own this book and I do not own it.

Thus it is a limited ownership that does not extend. As for the ownership of Allah Almighty, it is absolute ownership: He disposes of His property as He wills, and it is general and comprehensive. Is that not so? Allah Almighty sends down diseases and sends down wounds upon His creatures, does He not? Does not Allah test a person, so that wounds appear on him that pain and disturb him, and aches in his nerves and in his bones? If any of the created beings wished to do that, it would be forbidden and not permissible. But Allah Almighty has the right to do whatever He wills: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23].

So He said: Allah is the Lord, and He is the one to whom dominion belongs, and this dominion also encompasses essences and substances and encompasses the disposal of them, including the disposal in judgment. The legal rulings are received only from Allah Almighty, and it is obligatory for us to believe in and apply all of Allah's rulings, whether they concern acts of worship, transactions, or personal status. We must apply all of them.

If someone among the people says: Worship is the right of Allah, so it is between me and Him, and I do not transgress what He has legislated; but transactions are the right of the human being, so he may transgress the Shari'ah in them. For me, I may turn away from the Shari'ah of Allah to the rulings of the tawaghit (tyrants). Is that permissible or not?

* Students: It is not permissible.
* The Shaykh: Pay attention, brother! Buying and selling (...). Worship is the exclusive right of Allah, I do not know how to dispose of it. Buying and selling is for me, for my benefit. Whichever buying and selling agrees with benefit and profit, I may do it: usury (riba), deception, cunning, everything. What concern is it of yours regarding me? This is our disposal.

* Students: The mosque belongs to Allah, in contrast to the Shari'ah.
* The Shaykh: The mosque belongs to Allah, and the homeland belongs to the people or to everyone; do not mind us. We say: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]. No one has dominion; dominion belongs to Allah Almighty, who disposes of this dominion as He wills, in permissibility, prohibition and obligation, and no one enters into that. Whoever says this, and acts according to the Shari'ah in acts of worship, but rejects the Shari'ah in transactions, we say: he is a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, and it is not permissible to leave him in this condition, because Allah Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers, truly﴾ [al-Nisa' 150-151].

Believing in some messengers and not others is like believing in some of the Shari'ah and not others, because the former is a division regarding the messengers, and this is a division regarding what was sent, and there is no difference. Whoever believes in some of the Book and disbelieves in some of it is in reality a disbeliever in all of it, because we say: even if you concede that it is from Allah and that He legislated it, you have disbelieved in it, and if you disbelieve in it, it is disbelief in all of it, and the Shari'ah of Allah does not divide.

From here we perceive the gravity of the matter in many lands of the Muslims, who make judgment among themselves by other than the Shari'ah of Allah, and who consider these man-made tyrannical laws better than the Shari'ah of Allah, and more upright for the interests of Allah's servants than what Allah has legislated, we seek Allah's protection. This is without doubt a deficiency in their intellects and a loss of their religion.

How can this newly invented tyrannical situation, based on deficient reason, be better and more beneficial for the servants than the Shari'ah of Allah Almighty, which He legislated for His servants, and He is more knowing of their interests and more wise in what guides them? Any person who has intellect, let alone faith, can never conceive in his thought that these man-made rulings that oppose the Shari'ah of Allah are better for the servants of Allah than the Shari'ah of Allah, except one who is deranged and insane, and Allah forbid. This is not strange among the children of Adam: those who worshipped stones in the Jahiliyyah were similar to these in foolishness. These also worshipped the opinions of others and preferred them over the Shari'ah of Allah. The saying that religion belongs to Allah and the homeland belongs to the creation, is it correct?

* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: This is a clear error. It is said: religion belongs to Allah and the lands belong to Allah: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-A'raf 128]. It is not yours. The earth belongs to Allah, the people belong to Allah, the religion belongs to Allah, and everything belongs to Allah. When it belongs to Allah, it is obligatory upon us to walk in the guidance of Allah, and Allah is the Granter of success (...).

The waw (و) is either resumptive (isti'nafiyyah) or conjunctive, in the sense of conjoining sentences to one another.

﴿alladhina﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause ﴿ma yamlikun﴾ [Fatir 13] is its predicate.

As for His saying: ﴿those whom you invoke besides Him﴾ [Fatir 13], the author said: (you worship), because supplication is worship, and one who worships Allah may include supplication in his worship, as prayer, for example, contains supplication and is an act of worship. It may also be supplication through the language of the state (lisan al-hal), because what does the worshipper want? Success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. So even if he does not say: "I ask You for success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire," he wants nothing but that.

Thus he is one who supplicates through the language of the state. For this reason we say that supplication is worship. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me﴾, after His saying: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ [Ghafir 60]. This indicates that supplication is worship.

Here He says: ﴿those whom you invoke besides Him﴾ [Fatir 13]. The author said: (they worship), they worship. This is either by worship as an action, such as bowing to an idol, prostrating to an idol, slaughtering for it, vowing to it and the like, or they call upon it with the supplication of request, not the supplication of worship. They come to the idol and to the grave and ask it for their needs and seek help from them.

So His saying: ﴿you invoke﴾ includes both supplication of request and supplication of worship.

I have said that supplication of worship is supplication of request through the language of the state. How do these people call? I say: they call upon them. They call upon these idols in two ways: either by supplication of request, or by supplication of worship, and supplication of worship is supplication through the language of the state.

He said: ﴿besides Him﴾ (i.e., other than Him, and they are the idols). The idols are sometimes referred to by Allah with the feminine form and sometimes with the masculine form. Here He referred to them with the masculine rational form: ﴿those whom you invoke﴾ is for the masculine rational. He described them in this way, although they are inanimate, dead objects, in order to condescend to these worshippers of them, and to mention them in the most perfect state in which they believe them to be: meaning, even with their perfection according to your claim, of being rational beings, they own nothing.

He said: ﴿they do not possess even a qitmir﴾ [Fatir 13]. ﴿min﴾ is superfluous (za'idah), superfluous. For this reason we say: ﴿qitmir﴾ is a direct object in the accusative, marked by a fatha presumed at its end, its appearance prevented by the occupation of the place by the vowel of the superfluous preposition. That is: they do not own a qitmir.

Qitmir is said to be (the thin membrane around the date-pit). We have previously mentioned that there are three things in the date-pit that are proverbial for their insignificance: qitmir, naqir, and fatil. He said: ﴿of qitmir﴾.

What proves that they own nothing is His saying: ﴿If you call them, they will not hear your call﴾ [Fatir 14]. ﴿In﴾ here is conditional, the verb of the condition is ﴿tad'uhum﴾, which is jussive by the deletion of the nun, and the response of the condition is ﴿la yasma'u du'a'akum﴾, which is also jussive by the deletion of the nun. That is: these idols, if you call them, will not hear your call. Even if you call these idols until the Day of Resurrection, they would not hear, because they are inanimate.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And even if they had heard﴾. The author said: (hypothetically), ﴿they would not have responded to you﴾ (they would not have answered you). That is, even if these idols heard your call, they would not respond to you, that is, they would not answer you, whether you say: "O Lat, O 'Uzza, O Manat, O Ya'uq, O Yaghuth, O Nasr," even if they heard this call, would they answer you? Would they say: "Yes, what do you want?" No, nor would they give you the sought-after thing either, even if they were silent... For this reason He said: ﴿they would not have responded to you﴾ [Fatir 14], which includes response by speech, that these idols would say: "What do you want?", and response by action, which is delivering what is sought to those who seek it. They respond neither to this nor to that.

The author's saying: ﴿they responded to you﴾ (i.e., they answered you) is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ [Al 'Imran 195], meaning He answered them; ﴿so let them respond to Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 186], meaning let them answer Me; and similar examples are many.

So response here means answering; that is, these idols do not answer.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Fatir 14]. Look, add to that: ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14] (your associating them with Allah; that is, they will disown you and your worship of them).

So the answering of supplication is negated from them, and despite that, would that they were safe from their evil. On the Day of Resurrection, in that great, well-known station, ﴿they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14], and they will disown you. This is the utmost of abandonment, because on the Day of Resurrection people are most in need of victory and honour, and these idols on the Day of Resurrection will humiliate them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another﴾ [al-'Ankabut 25]. Who says this? Ibrahim: ﴿And he said, "You have taken idols besides Allah only as a bond of affection among you in the life of this world; then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 25].

In this verse there is clear evidence that these idols possess no benefit for their worshippers. This is one point.

Second: they add to their worshippers humiliation and abandonment at the very time when they are most in need of might and victory: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14].

* From this noble verse is derived: the demonstration of Allah Almighty's power in causing the night to enter the day and the reverse, because no creature can do that, however great his strength.
* And from the verse: the demonstration of His mercy towards His servants, because in this entering there are benefits that are not obtained without it. We have given you an example previously concerning whom?
* Students: Those on the equator.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, those on the equator, who do not (...) have day and night. What do they suffer from illnesses, lethargy in the body, and lack of vitality?
* And also from its benefits: the blessing of Allah Almighty in subjecting the sun and the moon to serve the interests of His servants: ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon﴾ [Fatir 13].
* And also from it: the explanation of this great verse, or rather these two great verses, of His signs: the sun and the moon, and also the night and the day. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat 37], and the manifestation of signs in them is clear because of their perfect wisdom, power and mercy.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that the sun and the moon run, that is, they proceed. In this there is a refutation of the proponents of the new astronomy who claim that the sun and the moon do not move over the earth and do not revolve around it.

We have said that it is obligatory upon us to hold fast to this apparent meaning, as long as we do not find definitive evidence showing that this apparent meaning is not intended. In that case, we have room to contradict this apparent meaning.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that everything is precisely regulated, ordained and determined for a specified term, neither exceeding it nor delayed; because of His saying: ﴿for a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13].

This term upon which the sun and the moon proceed, the author says: (it is the Day of Resurrection). It is possible that we make it more general and say: they run toward a specified term even in the orbit. For example, the sun descends to the Tropic of Capricorn in the winter days, then moves from it little by little until it reaches the Tropic of Cancer. It cannot exceed this or that, because it runs toward a specific term, each day a fixed place of rising and a fixed time of rising. Without doubt this is running toward a specified term.

* And also from the benefits of the noble verse: that the doer of these things is Allah; because of His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13], and no one can do that. In this is a refutation of the saying of the naturalists, who say that the alternation of night and day and the sun and moon occurs by the necessity of nature, the nature of the celestial spheres.

He refutes them with His saying: ﴿That is﴾, meaning the doer of this, ﴿Allah, your Lord﴾.

* And also from its benefits: the generality of Allah's dominion over everything; because of His saying: ﴿the dominion﴾ [Fatir 13], and the (al) here is for generality. The rule for the (al) of generality is that (kull, "every") can take its place. If it is valid that (kull) takes its place, then it is for generality. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 2]: put (kull) in place of (al).

* Student: Indeed, every human being is in loss.

* The Shaykh: Indeed, every human being is in loss. ﴿Man was created weak﴾ [al-Nisa' 28]: put (kull) in its place: every human being was created weak. So if (al) can be replaced by (kull), it is for generality.

And here, ﴿to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]: is it valid that (kull) takes its place? Yes, we say: to Him belongs every dominion.

* And also from its benefits: the exclusivity of Allah Almighty with dominion; because of His saying: ﴿to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13], where the predicate has been placed first, though its proper place is later.

We have mentioned during the exposition the reconciliation of this verse with the affirmation of dominion for other than Allah, and we explained that there is no contradiction between them, because the dominion that belongs to Allah has its own nature, and the dominion that belongs to human beings has a different nature.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 35, verses 13–14 (part 3 of 3):**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whatever is called upon besides Allah cannot bring any good to its caller in any way, because Allah has negated every means by which good could reach him or harm could be averted. He said: ﴿They do not hear your call, and even if they heard, they would not respond to you.﴾ This refers to the absence of any good, and the failure to remove harm and evil. Besides that, on the Day of Resurrection they will disown the shirk (associating partners with Allah) of these people, and this is a greater harm.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a clear proof of the foolishness of these polytheists. Their foolishness lies in calling upon those whose calling is not worthy, those who, even if they were supposed to hear their call, would never respond to it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, such as will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calling?﴾ ﴿Who is more astray﴾ means: no one is more astray.
And He said: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?﴾ And what is the religion of Abraham? Listen to it: ﴿Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ This is the religion of Abraham: tawhid (affirming the oneness of Allah) and the absence of shirk. These people are fools; they call upon what does not respond, and what neither benefits nor does anything but harm.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever attaches himself to other than Allah will be disappointed in his hope. How is that? Because these idols do not benefit them in this world, nor will they benefit them on the Day of Resurrection.
So then: were they disappointed or not? They were disappointed.
They say: "We worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah." But they did not bring them near. They only increased them in distance. So their hope has been disappointed, and they have, may Allah protect us, lost both this world and the Hereafter.
As for His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association of them with Allah﴾: what type of disbelief is this? Disavowal (tabarru').
* It is derived from this that these worshipped idols will disown their worshippers on the Day of Resurrection, yes. Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will gather the idols and their worshippers and cast them into Hell: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be its certain entrants. Had these been gods, they would not have entered it.﴾ But they are not gods; they bring no benefit.
If you say: the one who calls upon these idols may be tested, such that it responds to him outwardly, in the sense that he calls upon the idol to cure him of a certain illness and he is cured, or to bring him a certain good and it brings it. What is the answer?
* Student: That has happened when the idols were called upon.
* The Shaykh: That is, the calling did not benefit them, but Allah the Mighty and Majestic made this thing occur at the time of their calling as a trial for these worshippers.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of resurrection (ba'th), based on His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association of them with Allah﴾.
* And among them: affirmation of the lordship (rububiyyah) of Allah, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾.
* And also among them: affirmation of Allah's knowledge and His encompassing of everything, based on His saying: ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is all-aware.﴾
Do we derive from it a refutation of the Jabriyyah (the determinist sect who deny human choice)? Yes, from His saying: ﴿If you call upon them﴾.
And do we derive from it that these idols are rational beings?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: But they were mentioned by way of assumption, and in describing them with their most complete attribute in their own view, which is reason.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verses 13–14 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, said, showing the perfection of His power and His blessings as well. He said: (﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾, meaning He makes it enter, so it increases, ﴿and He causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning He makes it enter, so it increases). Pay attention to the author's words. Does this agree with the apparent meaning or not? (﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾, so it increases.) What is it that increases?

* Students: The day.
* Other students: The night.
* Sheikh: Alright, let us see. The day rose and the night increased, although the pronoun refers to the nearest mentioned noun, which is the day, so it increases. This requires examination. But its explanation of ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ [Fatir 13] is that some of the night becomes part of the day. This is one explanation: that some of the night becomes part of the day. When some of the night becomes part of the day, it means the day has increased. It is as if he is saying: the night entered into the day and so it became day. Then what increases? The day. And the reverse is the reverse. But the apparent meaning of the noble verse is that He makes the night enter into the day, so that a portion of the day becomes night.

Now, if you say: "I have added this to the irrigation channel in this land." Do you know what the irrigation channel (sāqiyah) is or not? (...) in the land. The part that entered the channel made the land an irrigation channel.

So, I have made the night enter into the day: I made a part of the day into night. In that case, it is the night that lengthens.

The causing of the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night is undoubtedly a sign of the perfection of Allah's power, glorified and exalted, because if all of creation gathered together to cause even a small part of the night to enter the day, or the reverse, they would never be able to do it.

Then this entering is also an entering in an orderly manner. What is meant by "in an orderly manner"? It means that it comes gradually, little by little, so that human nature adapts to this entering. What do you think would happen if the night came in its full length all at once? For example, today the night lasted eight hours and thirty-five minutes, and the next night it lasted twelve hours and five minutes. What would the state of people be? They would be thrown into turmoil. But Allah, glorified and exalted, causes it to enter little by little. This is with regard to the disturbance.

On another point: if it entered like that all at once, you know that the reason for the length of the day is the sun's nearness to being directly overhead. When the sun comes close to being directly overhead, it must be extremely hot. That means this day would be in the depth of winter, and the day after it in the depth of summer, and this would be a great harm. But Allah, glorified and exalted, causes it to enter little by little, and this is part of the completeness of His power, wisdom and mercy.

Also, the entering of the night into the day, and the reverse, has a great effect on the climate, because the weather changes from severe cold over a long period to severe heat, also over a long period. Do you not know that this intense heat kills harmful germs in a way that none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, knows?

To give a simple example that we all see: when the heat becomes intense, mosquitoes die and no trace of them remains. This is why they are most numerous in the period between summer and winter. Likewise, the intense cold kills germs, and none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, knows the extent of this.

For this reason the scholars said: the people of the earth most afflicted by diseases are those on the equator and near it. Why? Because they have no winter that kills, nor a hot summer that kills either. This is an observed matter.

So, the entering of the night into the day contains several wisdoms. This is why He mentioned it: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and He causes the day to enter into the night﴾ [Fatir 13].

﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾ [Fatir 13], meaning: He made them subservient to His servants.

﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾. The sun is known, and the moon is known. He subjected them, meaning He made them submissive. Submissive to whom? To the benefits of the servants. For in the sun and the moon there are great benefits for the servants, which those with knowledge in this field understand: great benefits.

Allah has not explained to us the weight or the size of these sun and moon, because that is not beneficial knowledge for us (...). Ignorance of it does no harm, and knowledge of it is superfluous knowledge (fudūl al-'ilm). If it does not distract you from what is more important, then occupy yourself with it. Rather, He has explained the benefits that follow from the subjection of the sun and the moon. He said: ﴿And He has subjected the sun and the moon﴾ [Fatir 13]. By the sun there is day and night, is that not so? And also the ripening of fruits, and great lights. What do you think is made available to the world in energy after the sun rises? Much that cannot be counted, because it provides electricity, and it also provides softening of things, as things need softening and heat. Moreover, in recent times they have begun to extract great and enormous energy from the heat of the sun.

As for the moon, it has been subjected for us as well through the light it gives at night, and through the knowledge of reckoning it provides, the counting of years, and so on.

And if you want more on this, refer to the book Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah by Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him. He mentioned many great benefits of the sun and the moon, and others have also mentioned this. But a person will notice a difference between the research of Ibn al-Qayyim, for example, and the research of the scientists of nature, because the scientists of nature look at these things from a dark, pitch-black, purely material perspective, in which a person is not nurtured with a religious upbringing and does not recognise through them Allah's power and blessing. But when someone like Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, speaks about this, he always derives from it the mercy, power and wisdom of Allah, so a person, along with his knowledge of this vast body of sciences, finds within himself the fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, His exaltation, and love for Him.

He said: (﴿Each﴾ of them ﴿runs﴾ in its orbit ﴿until a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13], which is the Day of Resurrection). Each of which? Of the sun and the moon. ﴿Runs﴾ means it moves in its orbit. ﴿Until a specified term.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, likened the falak (orbit) to the whorl of a spindle (falakat al-mighzal). The whorl of a spindle is a disc with a rod at its top and at its base a stick around which the thread being spun is wound. Perhaps some of you have seen it. Yes, this turns, because the woman spinning turns it this way until it spins and tightens the thread. The falak here is the orbit for the sun, in which it turns, and for the moon, in which it turns.

In attributing running to each of them there is evidence that they move by their own essence and revolve around the earth. This is an observed matter: the sun revolves around the earth, and likewise the moon.

As for what the astronomers (ʿulamāʾ al-hay'ah) claim, that the earth is what turns and the sun does not turn around the earth, we deny them until there is a sensory proof for us, which would be a proof before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for departing from the apparent meaning of His words. Otherwise, our duty regarding these matters is not to depart from the apparent meaning of Allah's words, because Allah, exalted is He, is the Creator, and the Creator knows best what He has created, more than others. Is this accepted or not?

* Students: Accepted.

* Sheikh: Accepted. And because the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are the clearest and most explicit of speech, it is not possible for them to contain any complexity, neither verbal nor conceptual. Rather, it is clear and manifest in its meaning. And because the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are the most truthful of speech, it is not possible for Him, the Mighty and Majestic, to inform us of a matter that did not happen, or of a matter whose reality is contrary to it. And because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the most desirous of making things clear, meaning He loves to make things clear to His servants more than anyone. Recite His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [an-Nisa' 176], and similar verses indicating that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wishes to make clear to His servants what they may be guided by. So if He, glorified and exalted, is the most desirous of speaking clearly, or He is the most beloved of those to whom clarity is directed, that being Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then Allah, exalted is He, cannot say in His speech anything in which there is no clarity for us.

So we deny them and we say: You have lied that the alternation of night and day is due to the earth's rotation. Rather, the alternation of night and day is due to the sun's rotation around the earth, and there is nothing strange in that.

They say: How can the large revolve around the small?

We say: There is no objection. We agree with you that the sun is larger than the earth, but what prevents the larger part, or the larger body, from revolving around the smaller?

When we look at the Qur'an, we find that Allah, glorified and exalted, attributes this movement to the sun itself. Likewise, when we look at the Sunnah. In the Qur'an Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you see the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. And in the Qur'an Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, I preferred the love of good [wealth] over the remembrance of my Lord until it was hidden behind the veil﴾ [Sad 32], meaning: the sun ﴿behind the veil﴾. And in the Qur'an He says: ﴿He subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term﴾ [Luqman 29]. These are six places.

* Student: ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place﴾.

* Sheikh: ﴿And the sun runs toward its resting place﴾ [Ya-Sin 38], like ﴿each runs to a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13]. All of them indicate that these actions occur from the sun. If this were due to the earth's rotation, it would say: "And you see the sun when they rise upon it", because the earth turned and so we are the ones who rise upon the sun, and it is not the sun that rises upon us.

As for their claim that this is an address to people about what they see with their eyes, and the matter is the opposite: that is, when it rises according to what the eye sees.

In reality, it is we who rise upon it. So how do we respond to them?

We say: This contradicts Allah's command, and we cannot turn away from this apparent meaning except by a sensory proof, which we can present before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because Allah will call us to account, saying: Why did you turn away from My words to the words of others? The address is from Allah, glorified and exalted: ﴿when it rises, inclining away from their cave﴾ [al-Kahf 17]. ﴿Inclining﴾ means it bends. If this were due to the earth's rotation, then it would be the earth that inclines. ﴿And when it sets﴾: if this were due to the earth's rotation, it would be the earth that sets away from the sun.

As for the Sunnah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr when the sun set: "Do you know where it goes?" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3199) and Muslim (159 / 250) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] "Do you know where it goes?" He attributed the going to it when it set. If it were the earth that turned until the sun disappeared, he would have said: "Do you know where the earth goes, for example?"

In summary: it is obligatory upon us to hold to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, that the sun is what revolves around the earth, and that by its revolution the alternation of night and day occurs. This is the obligation, and it is not permissible to turn away from this at all, except when a sensory proof establishes otherwise, in which case interpretation (ta'wil) and redirecting the words from their apparent meaning become necessary. This is because we know with certainty that the Qur'an does not contradict reality. As for something they say by their assumptions and estimations, we do not agree with them on it, and it is not fitting for a believer to turn away from the apparent meaning of Allah's words merely because of their saying, never.

As for the question of whether the earth revolves or does not revolve, we say: we neither affirm nor deny it. It is possible that it has a revolution, and nevertheless the sun has a revolution.

They say: If you affirm the earth's revolution, it necessarily follows that you must say the sun is stationary. We say: That does not necessarily follow. It is possible that the sun has a revolution and the earth has another revolution, and there is no objection to that. But nevertheless we say: discussing the earth's revolution is among the superfluous knowledge that a person should not waste his time on, except for someone who needs to know it, as it is said they need it for guided missiles and similar things known to its specialists. In that case, if he needs it, there is no harm in his researching it. But if he does not need it, we say: this is a waste of time. What is the benefit of knowing whether it revolves or does not revolve? Praise Allah that He made it a resting place, whether it revolves or does not.

He said: ﴿Each runs to a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13]. The particle lam may be for purpose (al-'āqibah): that is, each runs until it reaches this term. And it may be that the lam means "to" (ilā), as it came in another place: ﴿Each runs to a specified term﴾ [Luqman 29].

In any case, it indicates that this running has an end, and so it is. This end was explained by the author with his words: "the Day of Resurrection."

His words: ﴿a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13] mean determined, known to whom? To Allah, glorified and exalted. It is known to Him and not known to us.

So these sun and moon are not eternal, but they are continuous, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant﴾ [Ibrahim 33], meaning continuing; but they have a term: ﴿Each runs to a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]. The demonstrative refers to what was mentioned of the subjection and the running. Pay attention! I say: ﴿That﴾ refers to what was mentioned of the subjection and running, or does it refer to the agent in His words ﴿subjected﴾?

* Student: The agent.

* Sheikh: So: that Subjecter is Allah. The one pointed to now is singular masculine, and the addressees are a plural of males.

Here we ask: what is taken into account with the demonstrative noun and the second-person suffix kaf? Is the addressee taken into account or the one being pointed to?

We say: as for the demonstrative noun, what is taken into account is the one pointed to. As for the kaf, what is taken into account is the addressee. Do you understand? So if you point to two men while addressing a group of females, or point to two males while addressing a group of females, what do you say?

* Student: Hadhan.

* Sheikh: No.

* Student: Dhānikunna.

* Sheikh: We say: dhānikunna. (dhānī) addresses two males, (kunna) addresses a group of females: dhānikunna. In the Qur'an: ﴿She said: That is the one you blamed me for﴾ [Yusuf 32], but here in the verse the one pointed to is singular masculine. The one pointed to is singular masculine.

[Addressing a group of males while pointing to a group of females.]

* Student: Ulā'ikum.

* Another student: Tilkum.

* Sheikh: Tilkum, correct? Tilkum or ulā'ikum? Both are acceptable.

Is the most eloquent form for the addressee that the pronoun follows the addressee: a plural of males if the addressee is a plural of males, a plural of females if the addressee is a plural of females, a dual if the addressee is a dual, a singular with a fatha if the addressee is masculine, a singular with a kasra if the addressee is feminine? Or is the most eloquent form always the singular?

We say: there are three dialects:

First: that it follows the addressee absolutely. This is one.

Second: that it is always with a fatha, meaning for the singular: with a fatha for the singular.

Third: that it is with a fatha for the singular in the masculine, and with a kasra in the feminine absolutely. How many are these? Three dialects. Do you conceive them well, or not?

* Students: Yes.

* Sheikh: The first dialect, which is the famous and eloquent one: that the kaf follows the addressee absolutely. You address a singular masculine and say (dhālika), a singular feminine (dhālika with a kasra: dhālika), a dual (dhālikumā), a plural of males (dhālikum), a plural of females (dhālikunna). This is the most eloquent.

Second: that you make it a singular with a fatha in the masculine absolutely, so you say (dhālika), whether you are addressing a singular, a dual, or a plural, but on condition that it is masculine.

And you say in the feminine: (dhālikī), whether you are addressing one woman, a group, or two.

Third: that you make it with a fatha in the form of the masculine always, whoever you address. So you say (dhālika), whether you are addressing a man or a woman, a group, a dual, or a singular.

Here Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13]. The one pointed to in the verse, ﴿That﴾: what is its type?

* Students: Dual.

* Sheikh: No. The one pointed to is singular masculine, and the addressee is a group, because Allah addresses all of mankind.

﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13]. The Lord (al-Rabb) is used in the Arabic language for many meanings:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 13–14 (part 2 of 3):

Among them: the Creator, the Owner, the Governor. Lordship (rububiyyah) means that Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Creator, the Owner, and the Governor. For this reason He said: ﴿To Him belongs dominion﴾. This is a declarative sentence in which the predicate has been placed first to indicate restriction (hasr). The meaning is: dominion belongs to Him alone, to the exclusion of anyone else. It is absolute dominion, encompassing Allah alone: dominion over essences and substances, and dominion over the disposal of these substances. He is the Owner of every creature, and He is the one who disposes of every creature.

If you say: How is the restriction valid, given that Allah Almighty has affirmed ownership for others, when He said: ﴿except over their spouses or what their right hands possess﴾ [al-Mu'minun 6], and He said: ﴿or what you possess the keys to﴾ [al-Nur 61], and He said: ﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission from among those whom your right hands possess﴾ [al-Nur 33]? He has affirmed ownership for others. How, then, can you say that this sentence contains restriction?

The answer has two aspects.

The first aspect: our ownership is not absolute ownership; rather, it is ownership restricted by the Shari'ah. For example, I own this bag, but I do not have the right to destroy it. Do I have the right to destroy it? Never, because it is forbidden for me to destroy it. I own this camel, for example, but do I have the right to torture it? Do I have the right to wound it? By Allah, I would love to wound this camel, but I do not have this right except by permission from the Shari'ah. For this reason, when the Shari'ah permitted branding, branding the camel, although it is harmful and painful to it, it was permitted. And when it permitted ish'ar (marking) of camels and cattle in the sacrificial offering (hady), it was permitted.

Do you know ish'ar? Ish'ar is to cut the hump with a knife in the sacrificial animal until the blood flows over the hair and the skin. What is the benefit of this?

The benefit is so that it is known that this is a hady. For this reason we do ish'ar to camels and cattle, and we garland (taqlid) camels, cattle and sheep.

Sheep are not marked; they are only garlanded.

It seems the brother says: What is taqlid? Taqlid means that we place a garland around the neck, and we hang on it old, torn sandals and the ears of waterskins (qirab). Waterskins are known; the singular of qirab is qirbah. The ears of waterskins, meaning pieces of waterskins, are attached to it. We hang this on the camel, cow or sheep. Why? So that it is known that it is a hady, because torn sandals and pieces of waterskins indicate shabbiness and poverty, a sign that this is for the poor. But our point, returning to the original matter: is our ownership of the thing restricted or absolute?

* Students: Restricted.
* The Shaykh: Restricted, yes indeed.

The second aspect: it is an inferior (qasir) ownership, meaning it is not comprehensive. For example, I own this bag, but you do not own it, and you own this book and I do not own it.

Thus it is a limited ownership that does not extend. As for the ownership of Allah Almighty, it is absolute ownership: He disposes of His property as He wills, and it is general and comprehensive. Is that not so? Allah Almighty sends down diseases and sends down wounds upon His creatures, does He not? Does not Allah test a person, so that wounds appear on him that pain and disturb him, and aches in his nerves and in his bones? If any of the created beings wished to do that, it would be forbidden and not permissible. But Allah Almighty has the right to do whatever He wills: ﴿He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned﴾ [al-Anbiya' 23].

So He said: Allah is the Lord, and He is the one to whom dominion belongs, and this dominion also encompasses essences and substances and encompasses the disposal of them, including the disposal in judgment. The legal rulings are received only from Allah Almighty, and it is obligatory for us to believe in and apply all of Allah's rulings, whether they concern acts of worship, transactions, or personal status. We must apply all of them.

If someone among the people says: Worship is the right of Allah, so it is between me and Him, and I do not transgress what He has legislated; but transactions are the right of the human being, so he may transgress the Shari'ah in them. For me, I may turn away from the Shari'ah of Allah to the rulings of the tawaghit (tyrants). Is that permissible or not?

* Students: It is not permissible.
* The Shaykh: Pay attention, brother! Buying and selling (...). Worship is the exclusive right of Allah, I do not know how to dispose of it. Buying and selling is for me, for my benefit. Whichever buying and selling agrees with benefit and profit, I may do it: usury (riba), deception, cunning, everything. What concern is it of yours regarding me? This is our disposal.

* Students: The mosque belongs to Allah, in contrast to the Shari'ah.
* The Shaykh: The mosque belongs to Allah, and the homeland belongs to the people or to everyone; do not mind us. We say: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]. No one has dominion; dominion belongs to Allah Almighty, who disposes of this dominion as He wills, in permissibility, prohibition and obligation, and no one enters into that. Whoever says this, and acts according to the Shari'ah in acts of worship, but rejects the Shari'ah in transactions, we say: he is a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, and it is not permissible to leave him in this condition, because Allah Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and intend to make distinction between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and intend to adopt a way in between. Those are the disbelievers, truly﴾ [al-Nisa' 150-151].

Believing in some messengers and not others is like believing in some of the Shari'ah and not others, because the former is a division regarding the messengers, and this is a division regarding what was sent, and there is no difference. Whoever believes in some of the Book and disbelieves in some of it is in reality a disbeliever in all of it, because we say: even if you concede that it is from Allah and that He legislated it, you have disbelieved in it, and if you disbelieve in it, it is disbelief in all of it, and the Shari'ah of Allah does not divide.

From here we perceive the gravity of the matter in many lands of the Muslims, who make judgment among themselves by other than the Shari'ah of Allah, and who consider these man-made tyrannical laws better than the Shari'ah of Allah, and more upright for the interests of Allah's servants than what Allah has legislated, we seek Allah's protection. This is without doubt a deficiency in their intellects and a loss of their religion.

How can this newly invented tyrannical situation, based on deficient reason, be better and more beneficial for the servants than the Shari'ah of Allah Almighty, which He legislated for His servants, and He is more knowing of their interests and more wise in what guides them? Any person who has intellect, let alone faith, can never conceive in his thought that these man-made rulings that oppose the Shari'ah of Allah are better for the servants of Allah than the Shari'ah of Allah, except one who is deranged and insane, and Allah forbid. This is not strange among the children of Adam: those who worshipped stones in the Jahiliyyah were similar to these in foolishness. These also worshipped the opinions of others and preferred them over the Shari'ah of Allah. The saying that religion belongs to Allah and the homeland belongs to the creation, is it correct?

* Students: No.
* The Shaykh: This is a clear error. It is said: religion belongs to Allah and the lands belong to Allah: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-A'raf 128]. It is not yours. The earth belongs to Allah, the people belong to Allah, the religion belongs to Allah, and everything belongs to Allah. When it belongs to Allah, it is obligatory upon us to walk in the guidance of Allah, and Allah is the Granter of success (...).

The waw (و) is either resumptive (isti'nafiyyah) or conjunctive, in the sense of conjoining sentences to one another.

﴿alladhina﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and the clause ﴿ma yamlikun﴾ [Fatir 13] is its predicate.

As for His saying: ﴿those whom you invoke besides Him﴾ [Fatir 13], the author said: (you worship), because supplication is worship, and one who worships Allah may include supplication in his worship, as prayer, for example, contains supplication and is an act of worship. It may also be supplication through the language of the state (lisan al-hal), because what does the worshipper want? Success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. So even if he does not say: "I ask You for success in Paradise and deliverance from the Fire," he wants nothing but that.

Thus he is one who supplicates through the language of the state. For this reason we say that supplication is worship. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me﴾, after His saying: ﴿And your Lord says, "Call upon Me; I will respond to you"﴾ [Ghafir 60]. This indicates that supplication is worship.

Here He says: ﴿those whom you invoke besides Him﴾ [Fatir 13]. The author said: (they worship), they worship. This is either by worship as an action, such as bowing to an idol, prostrating to an idol, slaughtering for it, vowing to it and the like, or they call upon it with the supplication of request, not the supplication of worship. They come to the idol and to the grave and ask it for their needs and seek help from them.

So His saying: ﴿you invoke﴾ includes both supplication of request and supplication of worship.

I have said that supplication of worship is supplication of request through the language of the state. How do these people call? I say: they call upon them. They call upon these idols in two ways: either by supplication of request, or by supplication of worship, and supplication of worship is supplication through the language of the state.

He said: ﴿besides Him﴾ (i.e., other than Him, and they are the idols). The idols are sometimes referred to by Allah with the feminine form and sometimes with the masculine form. Here He referred to them with the masculine rational form: ﴿those whom you invoke﴾ is for the masculine rational. He described them in this way, although they are inanimate, dead objects, in order to condescend to these worshippers of them, and to mention them in the most perfect state in which they believe them to be: meaning, even with their perfection according to your claim, of being rational beings, they own nothing.

He said: ﴿they do not possess even a qitmir﴾ [Fatir 13]. ﴿min﴾ is superfluous (za'idah), superfluous. For this reason we say: ﴿qitmir﴾ is a direct object in the accusative, marked by a fatha presumed at its end, its appearance prevented by the occupation of the place by the vowel of the superfluous preposition. That is: they do not own a qitmir.

Qitmir is said to be (the thin membrane around the date-pit). We have previously mentioned that there are three things in the date-pit that are proverbial for their insignificance: qitmir, naqir, and fatil. He said: ﴿of qitmir﴾.

What proves that they own nothing is His saying: ﴿If you call them, they will not hear your call﴾ [Fatir 14]. ﴿In﴾ here is conditional, the verb of the condition is ﴿tad'uhum﴾, which is jussive by the deletion of the nun, and the response of the condition is ﴿la yasma'u du'a'akum﴾, which is also jussive by the deletion of the nun. That is: these idols, if you call them, will not hear your call. Even if you call these idols until the Day of Resurrection, they would not hear, because they are inanimate.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And even if they had heard﴾. The author said: (hypothetically), ﴿they would not have responded to you﴾ (they would not have answered you). That is, even if these idols heard your call, they would not respond to you, that is, they would not answer you, whether you say: "O Lat, O 'Uzza, O Manat, O Ya'uq, O Yaghuth, O Nasr," even if they heard this call, would they answer you? Would they say: "Yes, what do you want?" No, nor would they give you the sought-after thing either, even if they were silent... For this reason He said: ﴿they would not have responded to you﴾ [Fatir 14], which includes response by speech, that these idols would say: "What do you want?", and response by action, which is delivering what is sought to those who seek it. They respond neither to this nor to that.

The author's saying: ﴿they responded to you﴾ (i.e., they answered you) is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them﴾ [Al 'Imran 195], meaning He answered them; ﴿so let them respond to Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 186], meaning let them answer Me; and similar examples are many.

So response here means answering; that is, these idols do not answer.

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Fatir 14]. Look, add to that: ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14] (your associating them with Allah; that is, they will disown you and your worship of them).

So the answering of supplication is negated from them, and despite that, would that they were safe from their evil. On the Day of Resurrection, in that great, well-known station, ﴿they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14], and they will disown you. This is the utmost of abandonment, because on the Day of Resurrection people are most in need of victory and honour, and these idols on the Day of Resurrection will humiliate them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another﴾ [al-'Ankabut 25]. Who says this? Ibrahim: ﴿And he said, "You have taken idols besides Allah only as a bond of affection among you in the life of this world; then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another, and your refuge will be the Fire, and you will have no helpers"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 25].

In this verse there is clear evidence that these idols possess no benefit for their worshippers. This is one point.

Second: they add to their worshippers humiliation and abandonment at the very time when they are most in need of might and victory: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14].

* From this noble verse is derived: the demonstration of Allah Almighty's power in causing the night to enter the day and the reverse, because no creature can do that, however great his strength.
* And from the verse: the demonstration of His mercy towards His servants, because in this entering there are benefits that are not obtained without it. We have given you an example previously concerning whom?
* Students: Those on the equator.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, those on the equator, who do not (...) have day and night. What do they suffer from illnesses, lethargy in the body, and lack of vitality?
* And also from its benefits: the blessing of Allah Almighty in subjecting the sun and the moon to serve the interests of His servants: ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon﴾ [Fatir 13].
* And also from it: the explanation of this great verse, or rather these two great verses, of His signs: the sun and the moon, and also the night and the day. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat 37], and the manifestation of signs in them is clear because of their perfect wisdom, power and mercy.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that the sun and the moon run, that is, they proceed. In this there is a refutation of the proponents of the new astronomy who claim that the sun and the moon do not move over the earth and do not revolve around it.

We have said that it is obligatory upon us to hold fast to this apparent meaning, as long as we do not find definitive evidence showing that this apparent meaning is not intended. In that case, we have room to contradict this apparent meaning.

* And from the benefits of the noble verse: that everything is precisely regulated, ordained and determined for a specified term, neither exceeding it nor delayed; because of His saying: ﴿for a specified term﴾ [Fatir 13].

This term upon which the sun and the moon proceed, the author says: (it is the Day of Resurrection). It is possible that we make it more general and say: they run toward a specified term even in the orbit. For example, the sun descends to the Tropic of Capricorn in the winter days, then moves from it little by little until it reaches the Tropic of Cancer. It cannot exceed this or that, because it runs toward a specific term, each day a fixed place of rising and a fixed time of rising. Without doubt this is running toward a specified term.

* And also from the benefits of the noble verse: that the doer of these things is Allah; because of His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾ [Fatir 13], and no one can do that. In this is a refutation of the saying of the naturalists, who say that the alternation of night and day and the sun and moon occurs by the necessity of nature, the nature of the celestial spheres.

He refutes them with His saying: ﴿That is﴾, meaning the doer of this, ﴿Allah, your Lord﴾.

* And also from its benefits: the generality of Allah's dominion over everything; because of His saying: ﴿the dominion﴾ [Fatir 13], and the (al) here is for generality. The rule for the (al) of generality is that (kull, "every") can take its place. If it is valid that (kull) takes its place, then it is for generality. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 2]: put (kull) in place of (al).

* Student: Indeed, every human being is in loss.

* The Shaykh: Indeed, every human being is in loss. ﴿Man was created weak﴾ [al-Nisa' 28]: put (kull) in its place: every human being was created weak. So if (al) can be replaced by (kull), it is for generality.

And here, ﴿to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13]: is it valid that (kull) takes its place? Yes, we say: to Him belongs every dominion.

* And also from its benefits: the exclusivity of Allah Almighty with dominion; because of His saying: ﴿to Him belongs dominion﴾ [Fatir 13], where the predicate has been placed first, though its proper place is later.

We have mentioned during the exposition the reconciliation of this verse with the affirmation of dominion for other than Allah, and we explained that there is no contradiction between them, because the dominion that belongs to Allah has its own nature, and the dominion that belongs to human beings has a different nature.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 35, verses 13–14 (part 3 of 3):**

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whatever is called upon besides Allah cannot bring any good to its caller in any way, because Allah has negated every means by which good could reach him or harm could be averted. He said: ﴿They do not hear your call, and even if they heard, they would not respond to you.﴾ This refers to the absence of any good, and the failure to remove harm and evil. Besides that, on the Day of Resurrection they will disown the shirk (associating partners with Allah) of these people, and this is a greater harm.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a clear proof of the foolishness of these polytheists. Their foolishness lies in calling upon those whose calling is not worthy, those who, even if they were supposed to hear their call, would never respond to it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, such as will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their calling?﴾ ﴿Who is more astray﴾ means: no one is more astray.
And He said: ﴿And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?﴾ And what is the religion of Abraham? Listen to it: ﴿Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾ This is the religion of Abraham: tawhid (affirming the oneness of Allah) and the absence of shirk. These people are fools; they call upon what does not respond, and what neither benefits nor does anything but harm.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever attaches himself to other than Allah will be disappointed in his hope. How is that? Because these idols do not benefit them in this world, nor will they benefit them on the Day of Resurrection.
So then: were they disappointed or not? They were disappointed.
They say: "We worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah." But they did not bring them near. They only increased them in distance. So their hope has been disappointed, and they have, may Allah protect us, lost both this world and the Hereafter.
As for His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association of them with Allah﴾: what type of disbelief is this? Disavowal (tabarru').
* It is derived from this that these worshipped idols will disown their worshippers on the Day of Resurrection, yes. Indeed, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will gather the idols and their worshippers and cast them into Hell: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be its certain entrants. Had these been gods, they would not have entered it.﴾ But they are not gods; they bring no benefit.
If you say: the one who calls upon these idols may be tested, such that it responds to him outwardly, in the sense that he calls upon the idol to cure him of a certain illness and he is cured, or to bring him a certain good and it brings it. What is the answer?
* Student: That has happened when the idols were called upon.
* The Shaykh: That is, the calling did not benefit them, but Allah the Mighty and Majestic made this thing occur at the time of their calling as a trial for these worshippers.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of resurrection (ba'th), based on His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your association of them with Allah﴾.
* And among them: affirmation of the lordship (rububiyyah) of Allah, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾.
* And also among them: affirmation of Allah's knowledge and His encompassing of everything, based on His saying: ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is all-aware.﴾
Do we derive from it a refutation of the Jabriyyah (the determinist sect who deny human choice)? Yes, from His saying: ﴿If you call upon them﴾.
And do we derive from it that these idols are rational beings?
* Student: No.
* The Shaykh: But they were mentioned by way of assumption, and in describing them with their most complete attribute in their own view, which is reason.

The Almighty said: (﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah﴾ at all times, ﴿while Allah is the Free of need﴾ from His creation, ﴿the Praiseworthy﴾ in His dealings with them).

﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah﴾ [Fatir 15]. This address is general, to believer and disbeliever, the righteous and the wicked, the young and the old, male and female: all of mankind. Allah introduced this ruling with this form of address, which is a call (nida'), in order to alert the listener and to show the importance of the matter.

It may be said: everyone knows that he is in need of Allah, but have we acted according to the requirements of this knowledge? No. ﴿Nay, indeed, man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq 6-7]. So Allah established this constant state, from which no human being is free, namely need of Allah, so that he would act in accordance with it, return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and ask none but Allah.

﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need﴾ [Fatir 15]: this is a nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya) which implies exclusivity (hasr), because both of its parts are definite. ﴿You are﴾ (antum) is a pronoun of definiteness, and ﴿the ones in need﴾ (al-fuqara') is marked with the definite article (al-), so it is definite.

﴿You are the ones in need﴾. And what of others than mankind: are they free of need of Allah or not? No, but since it is man who may see himself as independent of Allah, the need is restricted to him, as if He were saying: if no one is in need of Allah, then you are in need without doubt. If the rational human being who manages his own affairs is in need of Allah, then what of the beast? Is it not greater in need? Indeed it is greater in need of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, than man. But He addressed man with this because it is man who sees himself as having become independent of Allah and self-sufficient before Him.

Rather, some of the children of Adam have reversed the matter, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich﴾ [Ali 'Imran 181], and we seek refuge in Allah. So they reversed the matter, contrary to the reality to which the natural disposition (fitra) bears witness.

He said: ﴿O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah﴾ [Fatir 15]. The word ﴿to﴾ (ila) here expresses the end point: that is, your need ends with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; none but Allah can fill your deficiency.

Then He said: ﴿while Allah is the Free of need﴾ [Fatir 15]; that is, the opposite of need. Al-Ghani means the one who is independent of others, as Allah says in Surah at-Taghabun: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need﴾ [at-Taghabun 6]. Allah, the Mighty, possesses vast independence, and yet His independence is coupled with praise; hence He said: ﴿the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir 15]. He is Free of need and is praised for His independence, because He bestows it upon others. But among the children of Adam, a person may be rich yet not praiseworthy. If he is rich and uses his wealth to dominate others and boast over people, and does not fulfil what is required of him, is he praiseworthy or not? He is not praiseworthy. But Allah, the Mighty, is Free of need and Praiseworthy.

The word (hamid) may be understood as an active participle (ism al-fa'il) or as a passive participle (ism al-maf'ul).

As an active participle: because He, glorified and exalted, is the One who praises; He praises from among His servants everyone who deserves praise, and therefore He lauds His messengers, prophets and righteous servants, and to praise them is to commend them.

And He is also praised for two things: for the perfection of His attributes, and for the perfection of His bounty. So He is praised for the perfection of His attributes and praised for the perfection of His blessings.

Here we say: the Praiseworthy is praised for the perfection of His independence and the perfection of His generosity through that independence, is this not so? Because not every rich person is praised for the wealth he possesses, but Allah, the Mighty, is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir 15], ﴿He﴾ (huwa) is the subject (mubtada'), what is it?
* Student: a pronoun of separation (damir fasl).
* The Shaykh: a pronoun of separation. The pronoun of separation has three benefits. What are they? Explain this to me.
* Student: Allah is the Free of need; that is, none other than Allah, glorified and exalted.
* The Shaykh: none other than Him, Allah alone and no other, as we say: Zayd is the excellent one, meaning no other. That is one. What is the second benefit?
* Student: It separates the predicate from the attribute.
* The Shaykh: The separation between the predicate and the attribute; that is, distinguishing between them. The third?
* Student: Emphasis.
* The Shaykh: Emphasis. If you say: Zayd is the one standing, it is more emphatic than your saying: Zayd is standing.

So the benefits are three: ﴿And Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir 15].

Then He said: ﴿If He wills, He will remove you﴾ [Fatir 16]: a conditional sentence, in which the protasis is ﴿if He wills﴾ and the apodosis is ﴿He will remove you﴾.

﴿He will remove you﴾: that is, by removing you.

﴿And bring a new creation﴾ [Fatir 16]. ﴿Will bring﴾ (ya'ti) is strange in being kasra-marked, since it is an imperfect verb?
* Student: it is jussive (majzum) by the elision of the weak letter.
