ثم قال تعالى: ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ وَلَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا لُغُوبٌ﴾ [Fatir 35]: "He who has settled us in the abode of permanence, from His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein." فيها فضيلة أهل الجنة بإضافتهم النعيم إلى المنعِم به، من أين؟ ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]، فنسبوا الأمر إلى الله وإلى فضله ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]، وهذا غاية الثناء والحمد.

* ومن فوائدها: أن دار الجنة دار إقامة، كل إنسان لا يتمنى أن يزول عن مكانه منها، حتى من كان في الدرجات غير العالية يرون أنهم في أكمل النعيم؛ لقوله: ﴿دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ﴾. ومنها تأبيد الجنة لإطلاق قوله: ﴿الْمُقَامَةِ﴾ ولم تقيد بزمن.

* ومِنها؛ من فوائد الآية: أن بلوغهم إلى هذه الدار ليس بحولهم وقوتهم، ولكن بفضل الله عز وجل؛ لقوله: ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾.

* ومن فوائدها: إثبات الأسباب؛ لأن (من) هنا سببية، أي: بفضل الله، ففيها رد على من ينكرون الأسباب ويقولون: إن الأسباب لا تأثير لها، وإنما يحصل الشيء عندها، لا بها.

* ومِن فوائدها: أن الإنسان لا يدخل الجنة بعمله؛ لقوله: ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾. ولكن قد يشكل على هذا قوله تعالى: ﴿جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]، ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nahl 32]، وأشباههما من الآيات.

وقد جمع العلماء بينهما بأن الباء في قوله: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ الباء للسببية، وأن الباء في قول الرسول (peace be upon him): «لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ أَحَدٌ بِعَمَلِهِ»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673), and Muslim (2574) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] للعوض، يعني أن دخول الإنسان الجنة ليس بعمله؛ إذ لو أريدت المعاوضة لهلك الإنسان، لو أن الإنسان نُوقش في عمله بالإضافة إلى نعمة الله عليه لكانت نعمة واحدة تقابل كل العمل، بل لكان العمل نفسه نعمة يحتاج إلى شكر، ولَّا لا؟ لأن توفيق الله عز وجل للعبد..

The Qur'an verse is given here as Fatir 31–32 requires, and the commentary follows.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 31–36 (part 1 of 4):

He says: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾ [Fatir 31]. The sentence here, ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth﴾, comes in the restrictive nominal form (al-jumla al-ismiyya al-mahsura), and there are two ways of restricting it. The first: definiting its two pillars, the subject (mubtada') and the predicate (khabar). So "alladhi" (that which) is the subject and "al-haqq" (the truth) is the predicate.

The scholars of rhetoric (ahl al-balagha) have said that defining both pillars of the nominal sentence conveys restriction. The second way of restriction is the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl), which is his saying ﴿huwa al-haqq﴾ (it is the truth). The separating pronoun has the function of restriction, a second function of emphasis, and a third function of separating the predicate from the attribute.

He says: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth﴾. ﴿We have revealed to you﴾: revelation (al-wahy) is Allah, the Exalted, informing His prophets and messengers of one of His laws. This is revelation in the legal sense (shar'an). As for its linguistic sense, they said that revelation is informing quickly and secretly; that is, a gesture, a whisper and the like are called revelation. But in the legal sense...

Some of it is not revelation. Sometimes the Prophet ﷺ was asked about something and did not answer, and then revelation came down and he answered with a prophetic statement. An example is the story of Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who had entered into 'umra while wearing perfume (khaluq), and asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, but he did not answer him until revelation came [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1536) and Muslim (1180/6), from the hadith of Ya'la ibn Umayyah]. Sometimes he is asked about something and then revelation comes down concerning it as the speech of Allah, the Qur'an, and he conveys it to them ﷺ.

He says: ﴿alladhi awhayna ilayka﴾ [Fatir 31]. What is meant here is definitely the Qur'an, as evidenced by his saying ﴿min al-Kitab﴾ (of the Book). This is because "min" (of) is explanatory (bayaniyya), clarifying the vagueness in the relative pronoun "alladhi" (that which). The relative pronoun (ism mawsul) contains vagueness, so when "min" comes after it, it is explanatory.

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾ [Fatir 31]: (the Qur'an). "Kitab" (Book) here means "maktub" (written), because this pattern (fi'al) often comes in the sense of the passive participle (maf'ul). Examples are "ghiras" (planted), "bina'" (built), "firash" (spread out), meaning "maghrus" (planted), "mabni" (built) and "mafrush" (spread). So "kitab" means "maktub" (written). Written where? Written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), written in the scrolls that are in the hands of the angels: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it. [It is recorded] in honoured scrolls, exalted and purified, in the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾ [Abasa 11–16]. It is written in the mushafs that are in our hands. Thus it is written in three forms: the Preserved Tablet, the scrolls in the hands of the angels, and the mushafs in our hands.

He says: ﴿huwa al-haqq﴾ [Fatir 31]. ("Huwa") is a separating pronoun, and "al-haqq" is the predicate of "alladhi". So that which Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ is the truth. Allah emphasised this with how many emphases? With two emphases: the separating pronoun, and the definiting of both pillars of the sentence, ﴿alladhi awhayna ilayka min al-Kitab huwa al-haqq﴾ [Fatir 31].

His saying ﴿al-haqq﴾ means the thing that is established as true in reports and just in rulings. So all the rulings of the Qur'an are just and all its reports are true; there is no falsehood in them in any way, and no injustice in its rulings in any way. This is because when you contemplate its rulings you find that it gives every person his right; therefore it is just in its rulings. When you contemplate its reports you find them all true, and this is truthfulness in reports. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [al-An'am 115].

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly, hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾ [Fatir 29]. Have we taken up the discussion of it?

﴿confirming what is before it﴾ [Fatir 31]. His saying ﴿confirming what is before it﴾: the author said: (what came before it of the scriptures), meaning confirming what came before it of the scriptures, because the scriptures that preceded it are "before it" (bayna yadayhi). Do you not see that a man who is in front of you has gone ahead, and you say "the man is before me" (bayni)? Sometimes "ma bayna al-yadayn" is said of the future too, because it is also in front of you, as in His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], meaning their future and their past.

His saying ﴿confirming what is before it﴾: the manner in which it confirms the earlier scriptures is in two ways.

The first way: it affirmed them, that is, it established that they are true. The Qur'an confirms the authenticity of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and other scriptures, and shows that they are true.

Likewise, the second way: ﴿confirming what is before it﴾ because the earlier scriptures foretold it, so its descent is a confirmation of them. So it confirms what is before it in two ways. The first: that it confirms what preceded it, that is, it said that they are true and established scriptures, and it made belief in them obligatory. The second: that it confirms what they foretold, that is, it descended in conformity with what they foretold, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 196]. The Qur'an. "Zubur al-awwalin" means their scriptures, meaning that it exists in their scriptures and that it would be sent down, just as Muhammad ﷺ was likewise covenanted upon every prophet that they would believe in him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on this?" They said, "We affirm it"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 81]. The point is that its confirmation of what is before it is in two ways.

He says: ﴿confirming what is before it. Indeed Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [Fatir 31] (knowing of the hidden and the apparent). The connection of this sentence to what precedes it is that it conveys warning, admonition and encouragement. It is both encouragement and warning, because when He informed that this Qur'an is the truth, people divided regarding this truth into two groups: a group that believed in it and a group that rejected it. Is that not so?

To all of these we say: Allah, the Exalted, is Acquainted with you and Seeing. Those who believed in it, their belief and their action in accordance with what it brought will not be lost, because Allah is Acquainted with it and Seeing of it, and He will reward them for it. Those who denied it, their condition will also not be hidden from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will punish them according to what their denial, rejection and arrogance require. So the sentence, in relation to those who believe in this Qur'an, is good news, and in relation to those who deny it, is warning and admonition.

His saying ﴿Acquainted and Seeing﴾: ("khabir") is an active participle in the intensive form (sigha al-mubalagha). If you wish, say that it is a resembling attribute (sifah mushabbahah). The second is better when it relates to knowledge. The best thing to say about this is that it is from the category of the resembling attribute. Why? Because the resembling attribute indicates permanence, whereas the intensive form may indicate occurrence, and the occurrence of acquaintance in relation to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is impossible, is it not? The occurrence of acquaintance is impossible, because He has always been and will always be Acquainted.

So we return and say: it is necessary to make "khabir" a resembling attribute, because if we made it an intensive form from "khabara" it would give the false impression of renewed acquaintance and knowledge, and this is impossible with respect to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿Seeing﴾: the word "basir" may be meant to indicate knowledge, and it may be meant to indicate perception by sight, and both meanings do not contradict one another. It has passed with us in the principles of tafsir that if a verse may bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is interpreted by both, because that is broader in its meaning and more eloquent. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Seeing of His servants in terms of looking and sight, and in terms of knowledge. In regard to the apparent objects of perception, there is both sight and knowledge; in regard to things heard, there is knowledge: ﴿Indeed Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾ [Fatir 32]. ﴿We caused to inherit the Book those who﴾: first, the word "awratha" (caused to inherit) here governs two objects. Were their original forms a subject and predicate or not? They were not originally a subject and predicate, and on this basis it belongs to the pattern of "kasa" (clothed) and "a'ta" (gave). Where is the first object and where is the second? In ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾, "alladhina" (those who) is the first, and "al-Kitab" (the Book) is the second. Because who is the inheritor? Is the Book the inheritor of those, or are those the ones who inherited the Book? Those are the ones who inherited the Book. That is, We caused those whom We have chosen of Our servants to inherit the Book. And what is the meaning of "awrathnahum iyyahu" (We caused them to inherit it)? It means: We made them its inheritors. So those whom Allah chose, Allah caused them to inherit the Book, that is, He made them inheritors of it.

As for the word "al-Kitab": the author said (the Qur'an), but we should make it more general, because if we said that "the Book" is the Qur'an, and we said that it was inherited from those who came before us, then the Qur'an would have been sent down to those who came before us, and that is not the case. So what is meant by "al-Kitab" here is the genus, not the Qur'an specifically. That is, all the good that is in the earlier scriptures is present in the Qur'an. So we have inherited from those before us everything of good that they were given. The foundations that are obligatory upon every Muslim in every place and time are present in the Qur'an, but the laws that differ according to nations, and according to time and place, these differ from those who came before us. Something may be obligatory upon us that was not obligatory upon them, and something may be forbidden to us that was not forbidden to them: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'ida 48]. As for the foundations, we have inherited them from those before us. So the foundations, which are the mother of the religion, we have inherited from those who came before us.

He says: ﴿those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾ [Fatir 32]. ﴿Those whom We have chosen﴾ means We chose. It is derived from "al-safwa" (the choice part), and its original form is "istafaynā" (istaftaynā), but for a morphological reason the "t" was changed to "ṭ", so it became ﴿We have chosen﴾, meaning We chose them.

His saying ﴿of Our servants﴾: does the term mean general servanthood or specific servanthood?

Student: Specific.

Shaykh: That is, those whom We chose from among the believers, or whom We chose from all the servants? It appears that it is general servanthood, meaning those whom Allah, the Exalted, chose from among His servants who submit to Him in the universal sense (kawnan). By them is meant this nation, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Ali 'Imran 110]. So those whom Allah chose from among His servants are this nation, by the verse we have cited, which is in Al 'Imran, and by another proof from this very verse itself, because this nation is the last of the nations. Therefore it is not possible that what they have of the Book be inherited by others. They are inheritors, not those from whom inheritance is taken. If they are inheritors and not those from whom inheritance is taken, then they are the ones who were chosen.

His saying ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir 32] (by falling short in acting upon it), that is, by the Book, ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾ (who acts upon it most of the time), ﴿and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ (who adds to the action teaching and guiding to action) ﴿by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir 32].

Allah, the Exalted, divided this nation that He caused to inherit the Book into three divisions, and He began with the least and then the less: the least in rank and then the less. He said: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir 32]. The one who wrongs himself is the one who has neglected some obligatory duties or committed some prohibited acts. He abandons congregational prayer although it is obligatory upon him, leaves out part of the zakat without paying it, delays the hajj although it is obligatory upon him immediately. This is the one we say wrongs himself. Committing prohibitions: drinking alcohol, fornication, theft, looking with forbidden gaze. This is the one we say wrongs himself.

The original meaning of "zalim" (wrongdoer) is "naqis" (deficient), because injustice (zulm) is deficiency. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Each of the two gardens gave its produce and did not fall short therein at all﴾ [al-Kahf 33], meaning it did not diminish. Everyone who does evil has fallen short in what is obligatory upon him. Therefore every evil deed is considered a deficiency in what is obligatory on you, because what is obligatory upon you toward yourself is to look after it with its due care. You are responsible, and the first thing you will be questioned about is yourself. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1975) and Muslim (1159/182), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As]. He began with the self. Just as it is obligatory upon you to look after the interests of your child, your wealth and your family, it is obligatory upon you to look after the interest of your own self. Indeed it is the first obligation among the rights of creatures after the right of Allah and His Messenger.

So whoever commits a prohibition has wronged himself, why? Because he has deprived it of its right of trust, since you are entrusted with it and must look after it with its due care. Whoever abandons an obligation has wronged himself, because what is obligatory upon him is to do the obligation in order to fulfil the trust concerning himself. This is the one who wrongs himself. And among them is the moderate one. The moderate one is the one in whom no injustice to himself has occurred and who has not advanced in good. That is, he upholds the obligations and avoids the prohibitions, but he does not increase in voluntary acts, and he is not eager to complete the obligations in the most perfect manner, and he does not avoid the disliked acts. He is moderate, neither lacking nor exceeding. He prays in congregation and pays zakat without deficiency, but he does not perform voluntary acts or voluntary charity. He performs the obligatory hajj but does not repeat it. He fasts Ramadan but does not fast voluntarily. Likewise, in his dealings with people, he performs what is obligatory upon him in the obligatory manner only. He does not show leniency to a poor man, nor does he reduce a price or a value, but he walks in accordance with what is obligatory upon him. We say: this is moderate. He neither gains nor loses; that is, he has no reward except the reward of doing the obligation only. The third: foremost in good deeds. This one performs the obligations and adds, by the will of Allah, the Exalted, of good deeds, and he also performs the obligations in the most perfect and complete manner. In prayer, for example, he does not limit himself to one glorification (tasbih), but adds to it. He does not limit himself to al-Fatiha, but adds more. He does not limit himself to placing his hands in a general manner, but places them in their proper position during standing, during bowing, during prostration, and so on. We say: this is foremost in good deeds. He pays zakat and gives charity, performs obligatory hajj and voluntary hajj, fasts Ramadan and performs voluntary fasts other than it. This is the one we say is foremost in good deeds.

As for the author's saying, may Allah have mercy on him, that the meaning of ﴿foremost in good deeds﴾ is (adding to the action teaching and guidance to action), there is clear issue with this, why? Because teaching may be obligatory. If he performs obligatory teaching, does he become one foremost in good deeds or moderate? Moderate. And if he abandons it, he becomes one who wrongs himself. Likewise we say of guidance: if he performs obligatory guidance he becomes moderate, and if he abandons it he becomes one who wrongs himself. But what we have said is the correct view.

What do you say about the disagreement of the exegetes regarding this verse? Some of them say: "So among them is one who wrongs himself" like one who withholds zakat, "and among them is one who is moderate" like one who suffices with it, "and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds" like one who adds to it. Another says: "So among them is one who wrongs himself" is one who delays prayer beyond its time, "and among them is one who is moderate" is one who performs it in its time, "and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds" is one who performs it at the beginning of its time, that is, at the time when it is recommended to establish it. Is there a disagreement between the two views? No, there is no disagreement between them. This is called diversity of variety (ikhtilaf tanawwu'). That is, each of the two speakers mentioned one kind, so this is by way of example, and it is not considered a real disagreement, but an illustration. This gives the example of zakat and this gives the example of prayer.

His saying ﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir 32]. The author said: (by His will), is it the universal will (kawniyya) or the legislative will (shar'iyya)?

The apparent meaning here is that we give precedence to the universal decree (al-kawniyyah). That is, all three categories, the wrongdoer, the moderate, and the foremost in good deeds, do this by Allah's permission. Allah is the One who permitted the wrongdoer to wrong himself, the moderate to limit himself to what is obligatory, and the foremost to go beyond it. Restricting this to "by Allah's permission" prevents a person who is foremost in good deeds from boasting about it, attributing it to himself, and bestowing it as a favour upon his Lord. Allah says about some of the children of Adam: ﴿They consider it a favour to you that they have embraced Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favour to me. Rather, Allah has conferred a favour upon you that He guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat 17].

So if Allah has granted you precedence in good deeds, do not think that this comes from yourself. If you were left to yourself, you would be a wrongdoer to yourself, because of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it, and man bore it. Indeed, he has been a wrongdoer and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab 72]. This is the reality of the human being: wrongdoing and ignorance. But whoever Allah has favoured and guided, that is from His grace, glory be to Him (...).

Allah says: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ (﴿That﴾ means their inheritance of the Book, ﴿it is the great bounty﴾). Yes, Allah has spoken the truth. The great bounty, which no other bounty approaches, is Allah's gift to His servant of knowledge of this Book. This is the great bounty. It is not the great bounty that a person be given palaces, luxurious vehicles, beautiful wives, or many children. No. The great bounty is that this Book be inherited. Whoever inherits this Book in knowledge, action, and calling to it has attained the great bounty. Allah says: ﴿Say: In the bounty of Allah and His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate﴾ [Yunus 58].

In His saying ﴿That is the bounty﴾ there is a restrictive particle, namely the separating pronoun (ḍamīr al-faṣl), in ﴿That is the bounty﴾. We mention the separating pronoun here for whoever has missed knowledge of it. The separating pronoun is a pronoun that agrees with the context. It comes in the third-person form, such as (huwa), in the second-person form, such as (anta), and in the first-person form, such as (anā). Allah says: ﴿And say: Indeed, I am the clear warner﴾ [al-Hijr 89]. ﴿Indeed, I am the warner﴾ is in the first-person form. You say to the one you address: ﴿Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [al-Dukhan 49]; this is in the second-person form. The third-person form is common, and this verse ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ is one example.

So the separating pronoun is a pronoun brought in agreement with the context regarding speaker, addressee, and absence. Grammatically (min ḥayth al-iʿrāb), it has no place in the sentence's grammatical analysis (i'rab); it has no grammatical position. In meaning, it conveys three things: emphasis (tawkīd), restriction (ḥaṣr), and distinguishing between the predicate and the attribute (tamyīz bayna al-khabar wa'l-ṣifah). Three things. What are they?

For example, you say: (Zayd al-fāḍil). Is there a separating pronoun in it or not? There is none. Here (al-fāḍil) may be a predicate, and it may be an attribute with the predicate not yet mentioned. Could we say the sentence means: "Zayd the virtuous is standing"? Yes, it is possible, and then (al-fāḍil) is an attribute. But if you say (Zayd huwa al-fāḍil), it becomes certain that (al-fāḍil) is the predicate, and it cannot be an attribute. So it distinguishes the attribute from the predicate, making what follows a predicate and not an attribute. Without it, it would be ambiguous whether it is a predicate or an attribute.

This explains our statement: distinguishing between the predicate and the attribute.

It conveys restriction: if you say (Zayd fāḍil), does that prevent others from being virtuous? It does not. But if you say (Zayd huwa fāḍil) or (Zayd huwa al-fāḍil), it becomes certain that Zayd alone is the virtuous one.

Emphasis: there is no doubt that your saying (Zayd al-fāḍil), intending subject and predicate, is a complete sentence whose meaning is clear. But when you say (Zayd huwa al-fāḍil), it is as if you have leaned on it and added emphasis to it.

He says: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾. (Al-faḍl) means giving. Giving from whom? From Allah. (Al-kabīr), great, in terms of magnitude: it is great in its quality. We know from another aspect that it is abundant in quantity. So this giving combines quantity and quality. It is a great bounty in its essence and quality, and also an abundant bounty in its number and quantity. ﴿That is the great bounty﴾ [Fatir 32].

Allah says: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence they will enter﴾ [Fatir 33]. This explains the reward of these three categories. (﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾: (iqāmah) residence; ﴿they will enter﴾, in the three readings, with active and passive voice; the predicate of (jannāt), the subject). In the active voice: ﴿yadkhulūnahā﴾, and in the passive voice: ﴿yudkhalūnahā﴾. When they are made to enter, they have entered, correct? So the two readings are essentially one. But the passive form ﴿yudkhalūnahā﴾ indicates that they are given it honourably, so it is presented to them so that they enter it. But ﴿yadkhulūnahā﴾ without the passive form: a person who enters may enter honourably or may enter on his own. But when he is made to enter, it is as if it was presented to them as an honour so that they enter it.

His saying ﴿gardens of perpetual residence﴾: (jannāt) is the plural of (jannah). The scholars said: al-jannah is an orchard with many trees, and it was named so because it covers whoever is inside it. And Allah knows best.

﴿Gardens of perpetual residence they will enter﴾: (ʿadn) means residence. That is, these gardens are gardens of residence with no departure from them. Rather they abide in them forever. Yet none of them wishes to move away from what he is in, as Allah says: ﴿They do not desire to be removed from it﴾ [al-Kahf 108]. This differs from worldly gardens. If a person were in the finest of orchards, he would wish to move to something better and superior. But in the Hereafter, each of them sees himself in a place of residence and does not wish to move from it. There is no doubt that this is part of the perfection of bliss: that a person settles and sees himself in the most perfect state, so that his soul does not yearn for a higher bliss which would spoil his bliss. For it is known that if a person sees that someone else is above him, even if he is in a secure station and in a blessed position, his enjoyment is spoiled because he sees that others are superior to him.

He says: ﴿they will enter﴾ (in the active and passive voice, the predicate of jannāt). (Jannāt) is the subject; the clause ﴿yadkhulūnahā﴾ or ﴿yudkhalūnahā﴾ is the predicate. (﴿yuḥallawna﴾ is a second predicate.) It cannot be a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject, because their adornment with these things occurs after entry. If we said "they enter it while being adorned," it would imply that the adornment is at the time of entering or before it.

(﴿yuḥallawna﴾ is a second predicate.) Is it permissible for the predicate to be multiple? The answer is yes, and this is common in the Qur'an. Allah says: ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Owner of the Throne, the Glorious﴾ [al-Buruj 14–15]. The general predicates are how many? Four: the Forgiving, the Loving, Owner of the Throne, and the Glorious. So multiple predicates are permissible in the Arabic language.

﴿They will be adorned therein﴾, that is, in these gardens. ﴿with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [Fatir 33]. Here (min, "from/of") is said by the author to mean "some" (baʿḍ), which informs us that (min) here is not explanatory (bayāniyyah) but partitive (tabʿīḍiyyah). If it were said that it is explanatory, that would also have good grounds, because adornment is not restricted to bracelets. A person may be adorned with rings, necklaces, or the like. So taking it as explanatory is better than taking it as partitive. If you say "they are adorned with some bracelets," the adornment is not with bracelets, but with some of them. Yet I say it is partitive, because the bracelets mentioned here are only two kinds: gold and pearls, though they also have another adornment, which is silver. As Allah says: ﴿They will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan 21]. So if you take it as partitive, on the basis that the bracelets mentioned are of two kinds and a third kind is not mentioned, then the partitive view has merit. We have mentioned many times that when a word may carry two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is interpreted as having both. So we can make (min) here shared between being explanatory and being partitive: explanatory, because adornment is with bracelets and other things, so (min) here specifies what they are adorned with; and partitive, because two kinds of bracelets are mentioned and a third kind is not. ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [Fatir 33]. What do you have? (Adorned with gold.)

﴿of gold and pearls﴾: (min dhahabin) is genitive, undoubtedly, since (min) governs it. As for (lu'lu'), in my view it is accusative. Is it so for you? But his saying (adorned with gold) indicates that it is genitive, as in the second reading. Therefore, we should correct (lu'lu'an) and make it genitive, based on the Tafsir al-Jalalayn.

﴿min dhahab﴾ is genitive for you, ﴿and pearls﴾ [genitive]. Now, what is the evidence that it is ﴿and pearls﴾? Because he said (adorned with gold). If he intended the accusative reading, he would say "adorned with gold" in the accusative. So we say: (lu'lu') has two canonical (sab'iyyah) readings. One is accusative, ﴿walu'lu'an﴾ (and pearls), and on this reading it is coordinated with the position of (asāwir, bracelets): they adorn therein bracelets and pearls, bracelets of gold, and they adorn pearls too. The other is genitive, ﴿wa-lu'lu'in﴾, coordinated with ﴿min dhahab﴾: they adorn therein bracelets of two kinds, of gold and of pearls. Add to them, they adorn bracelets of silver, so their bracelets are of three kinds: gold, pearls, and silver. There is no doubt that a gold bracelet is beautifying, and it has beauty in itself. Likewise, a silver bracelet, and likewise a pearl bracelet. Each of them separately has beauty and embellishment. When the three are combined and placed alongside one another, a greater embellishment arises from them. No one can imagine how these three are combined: whether the pearl is between the gold and the silver, or the gold is between the pearl and the silver, or the pearl between them. What matters is that no one can now picture this arrangement. But what we believe is that these three are combined. As for how they are combined, Allah knows best. But we also know that combining the three adds further embellishment.

Know that the gold mentioned in the bliss of Paradise, and the silver and pearls, are not like the gold we see now, or the silver or pearls. Rather, it is the finest gold befitting the bliss of Paradise. Likewise, the date palms, pomegranates, fruits, honey, milk, wine, and the like are not like what exists in this world. Why? Because bliss is suited to its abode. If the abode of this world does not resemble the abode of the Hereafter, then the bliss of the Hereafter is not equal to the bliss of this world. This is from the rational perspective. From the transmitted perspective, Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]. And in the Hadith Qudsi: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3244) and Muslim (2824/2), from Abu Hurayrah.] This is clear. You can see now that if a poor man came to you and prepared for you the best food he could make, the best thing he has, and a wealthy man invited you and prepared the best food he has, you would recognise the great difference between the two, even though each of them offered all he could. Likewise, the difference between the bliss of the Hereafter and the bliss of this world. So gold in the Hereafter matches gold in this world in name, but not in reality. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "There is nothing in the Hereafter from what is in this world except the names" [narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa'l-Nushur (332), and Hannad in al-Zuhd (3), from Ibn ʿAbbās]. Only the names. As for the realities, they differ.

He says: ([min dhahabin wa-lu'lu'in] [Fatir 33], adorned with gold). His saying "adorned with gold" may be objected to by the author, since it may be said that pearls are independent, a separate adornment. The accusative reading supports this: ﴿and pearls﴾, meaning they adorn pearls. But on the genitive reading, what the author holds is possible but not definite. Are you with us now? Good. He, may Allah have mercy on him, holds that the pearls are not independent but set in gold, as is found in worldly jewellery. But we do not accept what he said. Rather, the apparent meaning of the noble verse is that the pearls are an independent bracelet, and the accusative reading clarifies this: ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls﴾ [Fatir 33], meaning they adorn pearls. So he made the adornment with pearls a separate adornment.

﴿And their clothing therein is silk﴾ [Fatir 33]. Having mentioned what is worn on the hands, he mentions general clothing covering the whole body, saying ﴿silk﴾. Their clothing in Paradise is silk. The silk of Paradise is not like the silk of this world, which is produced or made by the silkworm. That silk is susceptible to every blemish. Rather, the silk of the Hereafter is silk that bears no resemblance to any silk of this world at all.

﴿And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾ [Fatir 34]. (They say) means the people of Paradise. When will they say this? They say it after entering Paradise. ﴿who has removed from us grief﴾ that is present in the souls, namely distress or sorrow over what has passed, and fear, the distress over what is yet to come. Here, do we say that grief includes sorrow over the past and distress over the future? Yes, we say so. Likewise, in Paradise, all the sorrows and worries that befell them before, they forget. As in the authentic Hadith, a person is immersed in Paradise (dyed with one dye): he is immersed in it, and it is said to him: "Have you ever seen any evil?" He says: "No." [Muslim (2807/55), from Anas ibn Mālik.] All the evils, sorrows, and worries that passed are gone (...).

The first: the perfection of the one praised. The second cause: the favour of the one praised. This differs from gratitude (shukr), which has only one cause, namely the favour of the one thanked. Perhaps we will touch on the difference between praise (ḥamd) and gratitude (shukr):

We said praise has two causes, so it is more general than gratitude in terms of cause, since its cause is the perfection of the one praised and the favour of the one praised. Gratitude has only one cause, the favour of the one thanked. Which is more general? Praise is more general, because it is for this and that. Gratitude is with the heart, the tongue, and the limbs. With the heart: that a person acknowledges the favour of the Benefactor in his heart. With the tongue: that he thanks Him and praises Him with his tongue. With the limbs: that he acts in obedience and does not oppose Him. The poet said:

"Three things have made you indebted to me by favour: my hand, my tongue, and my hidden heart."

But praise is only with the tongue, since praise is describing the one praised with perfection, so it is only with the tongue. Which of them is more general in this respect?

* Student: Gratitude.
* Shaykh: So gratitude is more general in its scope, since it relates to the heart, tongue, and limbs.
* Student: Does praise relate to the heart?
* Shaykh: Perhaps it relates to the heart, but it is not called praise. A person who conceals within himself praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not said to have praised Allah, since it is not made manifest. Someone might say it is with the heart, but it is not apparent.

He says: ﴿And they will say: Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief﴾ [Fatir 34]. The author said: (all of it), indicating that the definite article here (al) is for comprehensive generality (istighrāq). The article (al) is for comprehensive generality if it is valid to replace it with (kull, "all"). Is it (kull) or (kull, with shaddah)?

* Student: What is the difference?
* Shaykh: The difference: (kul, unstressed) means of food; (kull, with shaddah) comes from "entirety."

If it is valid to replace the article (al) with (kull, with shaddah), then it is for comprehensive generality.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-ʿAsr 2]: this is comprehensive. ﴿Man was created weak﴾ [al-Nisa 28]: comprehensive. ﴿Men are in charge of women﴾ [al-Nisa 34]: no, this is not comprehensive, since not every man is in charge. Sometimes a woman is in charge of a man. So this is only to state the reality.

The author informed us by his saying "all of it" that the article here is for comprehensive generality.

(﴿إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ﴾ for the sins, ﴿شَكُورٌ﴾ for obedience) This sentence, as you can see, is emphasized with two emphatic particles: إن (inna) and the lam. They confirmed with this praise that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is forgiving of sins and appreciative of them. Here "ghafur" (غفور) is it an intensive form (صيغة مبالغة, sigha mubalagha) or an adjective of quality (صفة مشبهة, sifa mushabbaha)? It includes both. It is an intensive form, indicating the abundance of Allah's forgiveness of sins and the abundance of those whom He forgives. He is abundant in forgiving sins, since a person repeats sins several times and Allah forgives them. Are those whom Allah forgives many or few? Many. From another angle, considering that Allah has always been forgiving, we say it is an adjective of quality.
* Student: Forgiving of sins and appreciative of them?
* The Shaykh: For obedience, appreciative of obedience.
As for His saying ﴿شَكُورٌ﴾, we say about it what we said about "ghafur": He, mighty and majestic, has always been appreciative of the obedience of His servants and their compliance with His command. Among His appreciation is that He gives the one who does a good deed ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. He is also appreciative in the sense of an intensive form, because the more the deeds, the more the appreciation.

On the mention of the reward of the people of Paradise: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ [Fatir 33] (...).

The accusative reading: the adornment with pearls does not have to be bracelets, because the sense of the sentence would be: "They will be adorned therein with bracelets and they will be adorned therein with pearls." It is known that adornment is with bracelets and it is with other than that. Is this clear now? So on the accusative reading it is necessarily separate from gold, and then it may be bracelets and it may be other than bracelets. This is on the accusative reading. On the genitive reading it may be combined with gold: ﴿من أساور من ذهب ولؤلؤٍ﴾ [Fatir 33], so the pearls are inlaid, as the author chose, and it may be that the bracelets are independent; it is not fixed.

His saying: ﴿وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌ﴾ [Fatir 33] and similar verses indicating the bounties of Paradise: does (...).

﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]. His saying ﴿الَّذِي﴾ here may be an adjective (صفة) of what preceded, namely Allah: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ﴾ [Fatir 34], ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا﴾ [Fatir 35]. It may also be a new (isti'naf) sentence, meaning that it is in the nominative case by way of "qat'" (cutting off), because when the described noun is known and the descriptive adjectives are multiple, the second adjective may be cut off or made to follow, as Ibn Malik said:

"And if adjectives are many and they follow, / the one who needs its mention is made to follow" (وَإِنْ نُعُوتٌ كَثُرَتْ وَقَدْ تَلَتْ ∗∗∗ مُفْتَـــــــــقِرًا لِذِكْــــــرِهِنَّأُتْبِعَـــــــتْ)

If it does not need mention, cutting off is permitted.

﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا﴾ means: "who made us settle" (أنزلنا), ﴿دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]: "the abode of abiding" (دار المقامة). "Al-muqama" here means "al-iqama" (residence), so it is then a place-noun (ظرف مكان), or it is a noun of place/time (مصدر ميمي) to which the feminine ta' has been added. The abode of abiding (دار المقامة) is the Abode of Paradise, and it is described thus because its inhabitants remain in it forever, and because they do not desire to reside anywhere else; each one of them does not seek a change from what he is in, because he sees that he is the most complete of the people of Paradise. Yes, indeed, Allah has made them content with the bounty they are in, so that they do not aspire to a greater bounty and look down on what they have. This is unlike the people of the Fire, for each one of them sees himself as the most severely punished of the people of the Fire; because if he saw that others were like him or that others were worse than him, the punishment would be easier for him.

﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾: the "min" (من) here is causal (سببية), meaning "by means of His bounty," that is, His favor upon us, because if it were not for Allah's favor upon them they would not have reached this great station. Everything good and blessing a person has is from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, as He said: ﴿وَمَا بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ﴾ [An-Nahl 53]. So their settling in the abode of abiding is from the favor of Allah, the Exalted, and this is part of the completeness of their gratitude to Allah, since they acknowledged His favor to Him. This is unlike the one who, when a blessing touched him, said: "This is due to me," or "This is from my own knowledge," or what is similar to that.

(﴿لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ﴾ fatigue ﴿وَلَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا لُغُوبٌ﴾ [Fatir 35] exhaustion from fatigue) "No fatigue touches us therein," that is, weariness; and the meaning of "yamassuna" is "afflicts us," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿إِنْ تُصِبْكَ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِنْ تُصِبْكَ مُصِيبَةٌ يَقُولُوا قَدْ أَخَذْنَا أَمْرَنَا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ [At-Tawbah 50]. So "al-mass" (المس) means "to afflict." As for His saying ﴿نَصَبٌ﴾ (fatigue) and ﴿لُغُوبٌ﴾ (exhaustion), this is because there is direct fatigue that befalls a person at the time of the act, and exhaustion that is the effect of fatigue. Is that not so? When you engage in a laborious task, you become tired during it, then after it ends you become exhausted, meaning you become weak and inclined to rest and sleep. In Paradise there is no "nasab" (نصب), meaning bodily fatigue at the time of performing actions, and no "lughub" (لغوب), meaning exhaustion, which results from fatigue.

He said: (exhaustion from fatigue, due to the absence of obligation therein) This is a weak explanation (تعليل عليل), because even in this world, most obligation does not involve fatigue; rather some of it is rest for the body, rest for the heart, invigoration of the body and health for it. This is not the primary purpose of acts of worship, but it results from practicing worship, such as the invigoration and health that exist in prayer, in fasting, in pilgrimage. There is no fatigue in righteous deeds. Rather, we say: ﴿لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ﴾ is from the category of negative attributes which include the perfection of their opposite; so no fatigue touches us therein and no exhaustion touches us therein, due to the perfection of their bliss, their comfort, their delight, their joy, and what is similar to that.

He says: (due to the absence of obligation therein, and he mentioned the second, which follows the first, to affirm its negation) He mentioned the second, which is "lughub," following the first, which is "nasab," because "lughub," as we said a little earlier, is the result of fatigue. It is as if the author answered a question; as if it were said: "If fatigue is negated, then exhaustion, which is its result, is negated; so why did he not suffice with negating fatigue?" And it was said: "No fatigue touches us therein, and if fatigue is negated, exhaustion is negated." Is it clear?

He answered this by saying that it was mentioned in order to affirm its negation. This is what the author adopted, and there is no doubt that it is a good explanation. But perhaps we may say: a person sometimes finds exhaustion and laziness and loss of strength without work and without fatigue, and this is observed. Accordingly, the negation of exhaustion is not mere emphasis but a basic matter. How is it basic? Because a person may sometimes find exhaustion even though he has not been working. Have you not experienced that?

So we say: its mention is fundamental and not merely a matter of affirming its negation, which is not intended except for mere emphasis. The point is that the people of Paradise, due to the perfection of their bliss, are not touched therein by fatigue or by exhaustion.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَهُمْ نَارُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [Fatir 36], so He followed the mention of the bliss with the mention of the punishment of the people of the Fire, because the Qur'an is "mathani" (مثانٍ, oft-repeated/paired): whenever a meaning is mentioned in it, its opposite is mentioned along with it.

You will hardly find verses in the Qur'an in which a meaning is mentioned without its opposite being mentioned, because the Qur'an is "mathani," so that the soul does not overindulge in hope if the bliss is mentioned alone; for the soul overindulges in hope and then feels secure from the plan of Allah. And if the threat were mentioned alone, the soul would overindulge in fear and despair of the mercy of Allah. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentions this at one time and that at another, so that a person proceeds without leaning toward hope and without leaning toward excess.

On this matter the worshippers have differed: is it better that a person journey to his Lord between fear and hope, so that he is fearful and hopeful; or is it better to predominate hope, out of a good opinion of Allah, mighty and majestic; or is it better to predominate fear? Yes, there is disagreement among the scholars on this. It is narrated from Imam Ahmad that he said: "His fear and his hope should be equal; whichever one predominates, his companion is destroyed, because if hope predominates, a person feels secure from the plan of Allah, and if fear predominates, he despairs of the mercy of Allah. So his fear and hope should be equal." They said: "Fear and hope are like the two wings of a bird; if one of them drops, the bird tilts toward it and loses its balance, and if they are equal, the bird goes straight and its balance is upright."

Some scholars said: "Rather, this varies according to circumstances. When a person performs an act of obedience, let hope predominate, and that the One who enabled him to do it will accept it from him and reward him for it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ﴾ [Ghafir 60]; if you are enabled to supplicate, you are enabled to be answered; if you are enabled to act, you are enabled to be accepted. And when he commits a sin, let him predominate the side of fear and return to his Lord; for if the side of hope predominates after committing a sin, he will not repent from it, and he will say: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ [An-Nisa' 48], and he will say: 'Allah is Forgiving and Merciful,' and what is similar to that." So hope predominates in one state and fear predominates in another state.

Some scholars said: fear predominates in one state and hope in another state, but not with respect to deeds; rather with respect to the condition. If he is sick, let the side of hope predominate, because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «لَا يَمُوتَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَّا وَهُوَ يُحْسِنُ الظَّنَّ بِاللهِ» ["None of you should die except while he has a good opinion of Allah"][[Narrated by Muslim (2877/82) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ansari.]]. And if he is healthy, let the side of fear predominate. The reasoning, they said, is that the sick person's soul is weakened and broken, and he does not incline toward this world but is concerned with what lies ahead; so let the side of hope predominate, since there is no soul aspiring to this world and immersed in luxury; rather his soul has softened and turned toward the Hereafter. But if he is healthy, the soul now has greed and aspiration for this world and its extravagance, so let the side of fear predominate.

In any case, we can say: if there are causes by which a person fears for his soul from letting hope predominate, then let fear come first; and if there are causes that require a person to fear and despair of the mercy of Allah, then let the side of hope predominate. That is, if he does the causes of hope, let hope predominate, and if the causes of fear exist, let the side of fear predominate.

Before we enter into what Allah the Exalted has prepared for the people of the Fire, let us return to take the benefits, because we did not take the benefits of what preceded, is that not so? From ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِعِبَادِهِ لَخَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [Fatir 31].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, mighty and majestic, from His saying: ﴿وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ [Fatir 31]. "Wahy" (revelation, الوحي) is Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informing one of His prophets of one of His laws. This is the position of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah: that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, which He spoke truly with its letters and with an audible voice, but it does not resemble the voices of created beings.
* Among its benefits: the virtue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what? In that Allah revealed to him this mighty Qur'an: ﴿وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ [Fatir 31].
* Among its benefits: that the noble Qur'an contains truth in its reports and in its rulings; its reports are all true, and its rulings are all just.
* Among its benefits: that whatever contradicts the Qur'an is false; from His saying: ﴿هُوَ الْحَقُّ﴾, by which truth is restricted to it. "Restriction" (الحصر) is the establishment of a ruling for what is mentioned and its negation for anything other than it, and everything that contradicts the Qur'an is undoubtedly false.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: warning those who oppose this Qur'an and giving glad tidings to those who agree with it; and this benefit is derived from His saying: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِعِبَادِهِ لَخَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [Fatir 31].
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of these two names of Allah, mighty and majestic, and what they include of attributes and rulings: "Khabir" (the All-Aware) and "Basir" (the All-Seeing).
* Among its benefits: the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge and its encompassing even of what the servants do; from His saying: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِعِبَادِهِ لَخَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾.
* Among its benefits: Allah's knowledge of what the breasts conceal. From which of the two names is it derived? From His saying "Khabir," and perhaps we also say "and Basir," because "al-Basir" means "the All-Knowing" and "the one who sees."
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that all creation worships Allah; all creation, they are all servants of Allah ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِعِبَادِهِ لَخَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [Fatir 31]. So no created being has any right to any of the distinctive attributes of the Lord; rather all are humble servants of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Qur'an is a "kitab" (book), that is, written; it is written in the Preserved Tablet, written in the scrolls in the hands of the angels, and written in the scrolls that are in our hands.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتَابَ﴾ [Fatir 32].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that this Qur'an confirms what came before it of the books; from His saying: ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ [Fatir 31]. And it follows from this benefit that whoever believes in this Qur'an believes in the earlier books, because this Qur'an confirms them, so believing in it is believing in what preceded of the books.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: citing an actual occurrence as evidence, even if it is from Allah. That is, Allah, the Exalted, cites an actual occurrence to increase the faith of the believers. The basis for this is ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ [Fatir 31] according to one of its two meanings, namely that it has occurred in conformity with what you were informed of; for when you are informed of something and then it comes to pass, this is evidence of its truth, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ آيَةً أَنْ يَعْلَمَهُ عُلَمَاءُ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 197]. So Allah, the Exalted, cited the knowledge of the scholars of the Children of Israel as an increase in confirmation and as establishing the proof against the deniers among the People of the Book.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the mercy of Allah, the Exalted, toward His servants, in that He did not leave them neglected, but sent down to them the books by which they are illuminated on their journey to Allah, mighty and majestic; from His saying: ﴿لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the breadth of expression in the Arabic language, and that the intended meaning is the sense, not merely the wording; from His saying: ﴿لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾. For someone may say: "Does the Qur'an have a hand?" The answer is that this is from the category of broad expression in the Arabic language. Do you understand? And that what is intended is the meaning, and words are molds that indicate the meaning. The "qawalib" (قوالب) of a thing means its vessels in which it is placed. For example, if a decorated carton adorned with gold is brought to you, you infer from it what is inside and that it is something precious and good. So words in reality are molds by which one infers what meanings they contain, and they have no inherent meaning of their own—meaning, the words do not change by whatever composition they are in; rather they change according to compositions and context.

Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتَابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا﴾ [Fatir 32].
* Derived from this verse: the favor of Allah, mighty and majestic, upon this nation, in that He bequeathed to it this mighty book, which Allah described as the truth and as confirming what is before it; Allah bequeathed it to this nation, and in that is a clarification of Allah's favor upon us by this inheritance.
* Among its benefits: that this nation is the best of nations; from His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا﴾, and they are this nation. We also derived this from another verse, which is ﴿كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ [Ali 'Imran 110].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an allusion to the interval (الفترة) between 'Isa and Muhammad ﷺ. From where is it derived? From "thumma" (ثم), which indicates delay (التراخي), and so it is. We do not know of an interval longer than it in relation to what lies between the messages and the revealed books. It has been said that the longest interval was between Adam and Nuh, but this is something about which a person may doubt. However, between 'Isa and Muhammad, peace be upon him, there were about six hundred years. The interval lengthened so that the condition of people would become desperately in need of the sending of messengers; then the Muhammadan message came to a people in extreme need of message and revelation, and its mission would have a great distinction, in that it came like rain falling on barren land, so that it would be more receptive to it and more affected by it (...).

...خلقت له، بل معناها يختلف بحسب السياق، وعلى هذا فلا مجال، ما دام أن المعنى مفهوم فلا مجال، ولهذا تجد أن الكلمة في معناها المفهوم بالسياق لو أنك أردت أن تحولها إلى المعنى الأصلي ما صح (...).

في استخراج الفوائد من الآيات السابقة، من الآية (...).

الكريم أيضًا تقسيم هذه الأمة إلى ثلاثة أقسام: ظالم لنفسه ومقتصد وسابق بالخيرات.

* ومنها، أي من فوائدها: الرد على الخوارج (Khawarij, a early sect that declared grave sinners to be disbelievers) والمعتزلة (Mu'tazilah, a rationalist theological school); لقوله: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾ [Fatir 32]، وجعلهم من الذين اصطفاهم الله تعالى من عباده، ولو خرجوا من الإسلام لم يكونوا من المصطفين. قد يقول قائل: يمكن أن يعارض الخوارج والمعتزلة هذا الاستدلال بأن يقولوا: إن المراد بالظلم هنا ما دون الكبائر، فيقال: إن ما دون الكبائر يقع مغفورًا بفعل الطاعات؛ كالصلوات الخمس والجمعة إلى الجمعة ورمضان إلى رمضان، وحينئذ ينتفي الظلم بمجرد فعل هذه الطاعات.

ثم نقول قولًا آخر بأن الآية مطلقة تشمل الظلم الأصغر والظلم الأكبر، ففيها رد على الخوارج والمعتزلة الذين يكفرون أو يخرجون الإنسان بالكبيرة من الإسلام، وحينئذ لا يكون من العباد الذين اصطفوا.

* ومن فوائد الآية الكريمة: أن كل عمل يقوم به الإنسان فهو بإذن الله عز وجل وإرادته؛ لقوله: ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Fatir 32]. وفيها الرد على القدرية (Qadariyyah, who denied divine predestination of human acts) الذين يقولون: إن الإنسان مستقل بعمله؛ يقول ويفعل ويترك بغير إذن الله، بل هو مستقل بمشيئته وفعله.

* ومِن فوائدها أيضًا: كبح النفس عن الاستعلاء والفخر بالطاعة؛ لقوله: ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Fatir 32]، حتى لا يقول الإنسان: فعلت ذلك من نفسي وأنا الذي فعلت وفعلت. وهذا خلافًا لما يسير عليه بعض الناس، إذا فعل المعصية كان جبريًّا (Jabari, one who holds that man is compelled in his acts)، وإذا فعل الطاعة كان قدريًّا، إذا فعل الطاعة قال: هذا مني وأنا الذي فعلت وأنا الذي فعلت، وإذا فعل المعصية قال: هذا من الله وأنا مجبر عليه. فبعض الناس يسلك هذا المسلك، وهذا مسلك بعيد من العدل.

* ومِن فوائد الآية الكريمة: إثبات عموم مشيئة الله عز وجل حتى في أفعال العبد؛ لقوله: ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ [Fatir 32].

* ومن فوائدها: تفاضل الناس في العمل، ويتفرع عليه تفاضلهم في الإيمان. أين الدليل على تفاضلهم في العمل؟ تقسيمهم إلى ثلاثة أقسام، ويلزم من تفاضلهم في العمل أن يتفاضلوا في الإيمان، فيكون في ذلك دليل لمذهب أهل السنة والجماعة (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, the orthodox Sunni community) القائلين بزيادة الإيمان ونقص الإيمان.

* ومن فوائد الآية الكريمة: أن أكبر فضل يتفضل الله به على عبده أن يوفقه للقيام بطاعته؛ لقوله: ﴿ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ﴾ [Fatir 32]. وقد أشار الله تعالى إلى هذا المعنى في قوله: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ [Yunus 58]: "Say: By the bounty of Allah and by His mercy — so in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."

* ومِن فوائدها أيضًا: أن إفضال الله على عباده يتفاضل؛ فمنه الكبير ومنه الصغير، وهذا أمر مشاهد؛ ففضل الله على الرسل أعلى من فضله على الأنبياء، وعلى الأنبياء أعلى من فضله على الصديقين، وعلى الصديقين أعلى من فضله على الشهداء، وعلى الشهداء أعلى من الصالحين، وهذا لا شك فيه.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ [Fatir 33] إلى آخره.

* مِن فوائد الآية الكريمة: أن جزاء أولئك القوم الذين أورثوا الكتاب على اختلاف طبقاتهم الثلاث أن جزاءهم جنات عدن؛ لقوله: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾، أو ﴿يُدْخَلُونها﴾، على قراءتين. ومنها الإشارة إلى كمال نعيم الجنة؛ لكونها جنات بهيجة، وكونها محل إقامة لا ظعن منها أبدًا؛ لقوله: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾.

* ومن فوائدِها أيضًا: ما ينعم الله به على عباده في هذه الجنات من أنواع الفواكه والمطاعم؛ لدخوله في كلمة ﴿جَنَّاتُ﴾، وكذلك من الملابس؛ لقوله: ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤًا﴾ [Fatir 33].

* ومِن فوائدها: أن الجنة ليست دار تكليف، أي: دارًا يمنع منها العبد مما يتنعم به، بل يتنعم بكل ما شاء؛ لأننا نعلم جميعًا أن تحلي الرجال في الدنيا بالذهب ممنوع وحرام، لكنه في الجنة مباح وممنوح وليس بممنوع؛ لأن الجنة لهم فيها ما يشاءون، بل أكثر مما يشاءون ويريدون.

ومنها ما يحصل من الجمال لتنويع الحلي؛ لكونه من ذهب ولؤلؤ، وفي الآية الأخرى فضة. وهنا لم يذكر الله تعالى تحديد هذه الحلية، لكن جاءت بها السنة، حيث قال النبي (peace be upon him): «تَبْلُغُ الْحِلْيَةُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِ حَيْثُ يَبْلُغُ الْوُضُوءَ»[[Narrated by Muslim (250 / 40) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]]. ومنها نعومة لباسهم وأنه أنعم ما يكون من اللباس؛ لقوله: ﴿وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌ﴾ [Fatir 33]: حرير لا يخلق ولا يتدنس، بل هو دائمًا على جدته ونظافته.

ثم قال الله تعالى: ﴿وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾ [Fatir 34].

* مِن فوائد الآية الكريمة: فضيلة أهل الجنة في ثنائهم على ربهم في قولهم: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ﴾.

* ومن فوائدها أيضًا: أن حمد الله تعالى يكون على إنعامه وإفضاله وعلى كمال صفاته، فهنا قالوا: ﴿الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾، فحمدوا الله على إنعامه عليهم وعلى كونه غفورًا شكورًا.

* ومن فوائد الآية الكريمة: كمال الفرح والسرور لأهل الجنة؛ لقولهم: ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ﴾؛ فإن هذه الصفة السلبية تدل على كمال ضدها، فإذا كان الحزن منفيًّا عنهم كان ذلك دليلًا على كمال سرورهم وأنه سرور لا يشاب بحزن أبدًا، بخلاف سرور الدنيا؛ فإن سرور الدنيا مهما عظم مشوب بالكدر، ولهذا يقول الشاعر الحكيم:

Life has no sweetness while its pleasures are clouded
By remembering death and old age.

نعم، الإنسان مهما كان في الدنيا من النعيم فإنه إذا تذكر أن أمامه شيئين لا بد منهما، لا بد من أحدهما قطعًا، فإن طالت به الحياة فلا بد من الأمرين جميعًا، وهو الهرم والموت، وحينئذ تتنغص عليه حياته. ثم هو أيضًا يعرف أنه كل يوم يمضي عليه فإنه يبعده من الدنيا ويقربه من الآخرة، وهذا تنغيص آخر، ولهذا قال الشاعر:

A man rejoices in the days that pass him by,
Yet every day that passes brings him nearer to his term.

نعم، على كل حال في الآخرة نعيم لا كدر فيه؛ لقوله: ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ﴾ [Fatir 34].

* ومِن فوائدِها: أن نعيم الآخرة ينسي كل ما سبقه من حزن؛ لقوله: ﴿أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ﴾ [Fatir 34]، وذهاب الحزن هنا ذهاب لما قد وُجد ولما يُتوقع وجوده، فلا يمكن أن يمسه فيها حزن.

* ومِن فوائد الآية الكريمة: إثبات اسمين من أسماء الله، وهما الغفور والشكور؛ الغفور في جانب المعاصي والشكور في جانب الطاعات. أما في المعاصي فإنه عز وجل قال في الحديث القدسي: «يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ، لَوْ بَلَغَتْ ذُنُوبُكَ عَنَانَ السَّمَاءِ، ثُمَّ لَقِيتَنِي لَا تُشْرِكُ بِي شَيْئًا لَغَفَرْتُ لَكَ»[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3540), and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (4305) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]].

أما في الطاعات فإن الله تعالى يقول: ﴿مَنْ جَاءَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾ [al-An'am 160]، وقال النبي (peace be upon him): «إِنَّ فَاعِلَ الْحَسَنَةِ تُكْتَبُ لَهُ عَشْرُ حَسَنَاتٍ إِلَى سَبْعِ مِئَةِ ضِعْفٍ، إِلَى أَضْعَافٍ كَثِيرَةٍ»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6491), and Muslim (131 / 207) from the hadith of Ibn Abbas.]].

ثم قال تعالى: ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا نَصَبٌ وَلَا يَمَسُّنَا فِيهَا لُغُوبٌ﴾ [Fatir 35]: "He who has settled us in the abode of permanence, from His bounty; no fatigue touches us therein, nor does weariness touch us therein." فيها فضيلة أهل الجنة بإضافتهم النعيم إلى المنعِم به، من أين؟ ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]، فنسبوا الأمر إلى الله وإلى فضله ﴿الَّذِي أَحَلَّنَا دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ [Fatir 35]، وهذا غاية الثناء والحمد.

* ومن فوائدها: أن دار الجنة دار إقامة، كل إنسان لا يتمنى أن يزول عن مكانه منها، حتى من كان في الدرجات غير العالية يرون أنهم في أكمل النعيم؛ لقوله: ﴿دَارَ الْمُقَامَةِ﴾. ومنها تأبيد الجنة لإطلاق قوله: ﴿الْمُقَامَةِ﴾ ولم تقيد بزمن.

* ومِنها؛ من فوائد الآية: أن بلوغهم إلى هذه الدار ليس بحولهم وقوتهم، ولكن بفضل الله عز وجل؛ لقوله: ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾.

* ومن فوائدها: إثبات الأسباب؛ لأن (من) هنا سببية، أي: بفضل الله، ففيها رد على من ينكرون الأسباب ويقولون: إن الأسباب لا تأثير لها، وإنما يحصل الشيء عندها، لا بها.

* ومِن فوائدها: أن الإنسان لا يدخل الجنة بعمله؛ لقوله: ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾. ولكن قد يشكل على هذا قوله تعالى: ﴿جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Sajdah 17]، ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [al-Nahl 32]، وأشباههما من الآيات.

وقد جمع العلماء بينهما بأن الباء في قوله: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ الباء للسببية، وأن الباء في قول الرسول (peace be upon him): «لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ أَحَدٌ بِعَمَلِهِ»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5673), and Muslim (2574) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]] للعوض، يعني أن دخول الإنسان الجنة ليس بعمله؛ إذ لو أريدت المعاوضة لهلك الإنسان، لو أن الإنسان نُوقش في عمله بالإضافة إلى نعمة الله عليه لكانت نعمة واحدة تقابل كل العمل، بل لكان العمل نفسه نعمة يحتاج إلى شكر، ولَّا لا؟ لأن توفيق الله عز وجل للعبد..

The Qur'an verse is given here as Fatir 31–32 requires, and the commentary follows.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 31–36 (part 1 of 4):

He says: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾ [Fatir 31]. The sentence here, ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth﴾, comes in the restrictive nominal form (al-jumla al-ismiyya al-mahsura), and there are two ways of restricting it. The first: definiting its two pillars, the subject (mubtada') and the predicate (khabar). So "alladhi" (that which) is the subject and "al-haqq" (the truth) is the predicate.

The scholars of rhetoric (ahl al-balagha) have said that defining both pillars of the nominal sentence conveys restriction. The second way of restriction is the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl), which is his saying ﴿huwa al-haqq﴾ (it is the truth). The separating pronoun has the function of restriction, a second function of emphasis, and a third function of separating the predicate from the attribute.

He says: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth﴾. ﴿We have revealed to you﴾: revelation (al-wahy) is Allah, the Exalted, informing His prophets and messengers of one of His laws. This is revelation in the legal sense (shar'an). As for its linguistic sense, they said that revelation is informing quickly and secretly; that is, a gesture, a whisper and the like are called revelation. But in the legal sense...

Some of it is not revelation. Sometimes the Prophet ﷺ was asked about something and did not answer, and then revelation came down and he answered with a prophetic statement. An example is the story of Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who had entered into 'umra while wearing perfume (khaluq), and asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, but he did not answer him until revelation came [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1536) and Muslim (1180/6), from the hadith of Ya'la ibn Umayyah]. Sometimes he is asked about something and then revelation comes down concerning it as the speech of Allah, the Qur'an, and he conveys it to them ﷺ.

He says: ﴿alladhi awhayna ilayka﴾ [Fatir 31]. What is meant here is definitely the Qur'an, as evidenced by his saying ﴿min al-Kitab﴾ (of the Book). This is because "min" (of) is explanatory (bayaniyya), clarifying the vagueness in the relative pronoun "alladhi" (that which). The relative pronoun (ism mawsul) contains vagueness, so when "min" comes after it, it is explanatory.

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾ [Fatir 31]: (the Qur'an). "Kitab" (Book) here means "maktub" (written), because this pattern (fi'al) often comes in the sense of the passive participle (maf'ul). Examples are "ghiras" (planted), "bina'" (built), "firash" (spread out), meaning "maghrus" (planted), "mabni" (built) and "mafrush" (spread). So "kitab" means "maktub" (written). Written where? Written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), written in the scrolls that are in the hands of the angels: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it. [It is recorded] in honoured scrolls, exalted and purified, in the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful﴾ [Abasa 11–16]. It is written in the mushafs that are in our hands. Thus it is written in three forms: the Preserved Tablet, the scrolls in the hands of the angels, and the mushafs in our hands.

He says: ﴿huwa al-haqq﴾ [Fatir 31]. ("Huwa") is a separating pronoun, and "al-haqq" is the predicate of "alladhi". So that which Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ is the truth. Allah emphasised this with how many emphases? With two emphases: the separating pronoun, and the definiting of both pillars of the sentence, ﴿alladhi awhayna ilayka min al-Kitab huwa al-haqq﴾ [Fatir 31].

His saying ﴿al-haqq﴾ means the thing that is established as true in reports and just in rulings. So all the rulings of the Qur'an are just and all its reports are true; there is no falsehood in them in any way, and no injustice in its rulings in any way. This is because when you contemplate its rulings you find that it gives every person his right; therefore it is just in its rulings. When you contemplate its reports you find them all true, and this is truthfulness in reports. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing﴾ [al-An'am 115].

Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly, hope for a commerce that will never perish﴾ [Fatir 29]. Have we taken up the discussion of it?

﴿confirming what is before it﴾ [Fatir 31]. His saying ﴿confirming what is before it﴾: the author said: (what came before it of the scriptures), meaning confirming what came before it of the scriptures, because the scriptures that preceded it are "before it" (bayna yadayhi). Do you not see that a man who is in front of you has gone ahead, and you say "the man is before me" (bayni)? Sometimes "ma bayna al-yadayn" is said of the future too, because it is also in front of you, as in His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Baqarah 255], meaning their future and their past.

His saying ﴿confirming what is before it﴾: the manner in which it confirms the earlier scriptures is in two ways.

The first way: it affirmed them, that is, it established that they are true. The Qur'an confirms the authenticity of the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and other scriptures, and shows that they are true.

Likewise, the second way: ﴿confirming what is before it﴾ because the earlier scriptures foretold it, so its descent is a confirmation of them. So it confirms what is before it in two ways. The first: that it confirms what preceded it, that is, it said that they are true and established scriptures, and it made belief in them obligatory. The second: that it confirms what they foretold, that is, it descended in conformity with what they foretold, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 196]. The Qur'an. "Zubur al-awwalin" means their scriptures, meaning that it exists in their scriptures and that it would be sent down, just as Muhammad ﷺ was likewise covenanted upon every prophet that they would believe in him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I give you of Scripture and wisdom and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said, "Do you affirm and accept My commitment on this?" They said, "We affirm it"﴾ [Ali 'Imran 81]. The point is that its confirmation of what is before it is in two ways.

He says: ﴿confirming what is before it. Indeed Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾ [Fatir 31] (knowing of the hidden and the apparent). The connection of this sentence to what precedes it is that it conveys warning, admonition and encouragement. It is both encouragement and warning, because when He informed that this Qur'an is the truth, people divided regarding this truth into two groups: a group that believed in it and a group that rejected it. Is that not so?

To all of these we say: Allah, the Exalted, is Acquainted with you and Seeing. Those who believed in it, their belief and their action in accordance with what it brought will not be lost, because Allah is Acquainted with it and Seeing of it, and He will reward them for it. Those who denied it, their condition will also not be hidden from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and He will punish them according to what their denial, rejection and arrogance require. So the sentence, in relation to those who believe in this Qur'an, is good news, and in relation to those who deny it, is warning and admonition.

His saying ﴿Acquainted and Seeing﴾: ("khabir") is an active participle in the intensive form (sigha al-mubalagha). If you wish, say that it is a resembling attribute (sifah mushabbahah). The second is better when it relates to knowledge. The best thing to say about this is that it is from the category of the resembling attribute. Why? Because the resembling attribute indicates permanence, whereas the intensive form may indicate occurrence, and the occurrence of acquaintance in relation to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is impossible, is it not? The occurrence of acquaintance is impossible, because He has always been and will always be Acquainted.

So we return and say: it is necessary to make "khabir" a resembling attribute, because if we made it an intensive form from "khabara" it would give the false impression of renewed acquaintance and knowledge, and this is impossible with respect to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

His saying ﴿Seeing﴾: the word "basir" may be meant to indicate knowledge, and it may be meant to indicate perception by sight, and both meanings do not contradict one another. It has passed with us in the principles of tafsir that if a verse may bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is interpreted by both, because that is broader in its meaning and more eloquent. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is Seeing of His servants in terms of looking and sight, and in terms of knowledge. In regard to the apparent objects of perception, there is both sight and knowledge; in regard to things heard, there is knowledge: ﴿Indeed Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾ [Fatir 32]. ﴿We caused to inherit the Book those who﴾: first, the word "awratha" (caused to inherit) here governs two objects. Were their original forms a subject and predicate or not? They were not originally a subject and predicate, and on this basis it belongs to the pattern of "kasa" (clothed) and "a'ta" (gave). Where is the first object and where is the second? In ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾, "alladhina" (those who) is the first, and "al-Kitab" (the Book) is the second. Because who is the inheritor? Is the Book the inheritor of those, or are those the ones who inherited the Book? Those are the ones who inherited the Book. That is, We caused those whom We have chosen of Our servants to inherit the Book. And what is the meaning of "awrathnahum iyyahu" (We caused them to inherit it)? It means: We made them its inheritors. So those whom Allah chose, Allah caused them to inherit the Book, that is, He made them inheritors of it.

As for the word "al-Kitab": the author said (the Qur'an), but we should make it more general, because if we said that "the Book" is the Qur'an, and we said that it was inherited from those who came before us, then the Qur'an would have been sent down to those who came before us, and that is not the case. So what is meant by "al-Kitab" here is the genus, not the Qur'an specifically. That is, all the good that is in the earlier scriptures is present in the Qur'an. So we have inherited from those before us everything of good that they were given. The foundations that are obligatory upon every Muslim in every place and time are present in the Qur'an, but the laws that differ according to nations, and according to time and place, these differ from those who came before us. Something may be obligatory upon us that was not obligatory upon them, and something may be forbidden to us that was not forbidden to them: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [al-Ma'ida 48]. As for the foundations, we have inherited them from those before us. So the foundations, which are the mother of the religion, we have inherited from those who came before us.

He says: ﴿those whom We have chosen of Our servants﴾ [Fatir 32]. ﴿Those whom We have chosen﴾ means We chose. It is derived from "al-safwa" (the choice part), and its original form is "istafaynā" (istaftaynā), but for a morphological reason the "t" was changed to "ṭ", so it became ﴿We have chosen﴾, meaning We chose them.

His saying ﴿of Our servants﴾: does the term mean general servanthood or specific servanthood?

Student: Specific.

Shaykh: That is, those whom We chose from among the believers, or whom We chose from all the servants? It appears that it is general servanthood, meaning those whom Allah, the Exalted, chose from among His servants who submit to Him in the universal sense (kawnan). By them is meant this nation, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind﴾ [Ali 'Imran 110]. So those whom Allah chose from among His servants are this nation, by the verse we have cited, which is in Al 'Imran, and by another proof from this very verse itself, because this nation is the last of the nations. Therefore it is not possible that what they have of the Book be inherited by others. They are inheritors, not those from whom inheritance is taken. If they are inheritors and not those from whom inheritance is taken, then they are the ones who were chosen.

His saying ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir 32] (by falling short in acting upon it), that is, by the Book, ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾ (who acts upon it most of the time), ﴿and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ (who adds to the action teaching and guiding to action) ﴿by permission of Allah﴾ [Fatir 32].

Allah, the Exalted, divided this nation that He caused to inherit the Book into three divisions, and He began with the least and then the less: the least in rank and then the less. He said: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir 32].
