No one can turn any of these celestial bodies, stars, sun or moon away from their course except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor prevent them from their motion except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In the grammar here we said: the lam in "la-in" is the lam of oath, "in" is conditional, and "amsakahuma" is the answer of the condition or the answer of the oath?

* A student: The oath.

* The Shaykh: Yes, the answer of the oath. Why? Because we have a rule: when the condition and the oath come together, the answer of whichever comes later is omitted. Ibn Malik stated this rule:

"Omit, when condition and oath are combined, the answer of whichever you placed later, and it is then obligatory [to omit]."

So the one placed later here is the condition, so its answer is the one omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.

He says: (﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾: that is, in delaying the punishment of the disbelievers.) His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing﴾: this sentence's connection to what precedes it is that it gives the reason for what precedes, so its link to it is the link of cause to effect. That is, in His holding the heavens and the earth He was Forbearing and Forgiving, and were it not for His forbearance and forgiveness, the heavens and the earth would cease and whoever is in them would perish.

"Al-Halim" (the Forbearing) is one of Allah's names, and its meaning is "possessor of forbearance." Forbearance is delaying punishment from its deserving, delaying punishment and not abandoning it; for abandoning punishment is pardon, but delaying punishment for the wrongdoer is called forbearance. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"He is the Forbearing, who does not hasten upon His servant with punishment, so that he may repent from disobedience."

So by His forbearance, Mighty and Majestic, punishments are delayed, perhaps people will repent to Allah, Glorified and Exalted. "Ghafur" (Forgiving): this one forgives the sin and erases its effect entirely. We have previously mentioned that maghfirah is concealing the sin and overlooking it; that is because it is derived from the maghfar, the helmet that covers the head and protects it from arrows, and it is not, as some have said, mere concealment, because mere concealment does not achieve protection; rather, protection must accompany concealment. This meaning is supported by the saying of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, in the Qudsi hadith, to His servant when He speaks privately with him and makes him confess his sins, He says: "I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441), and Muslim (2768 / 52), from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] This indicates that concealment is other than forgiveness, and that forgiveness requires the absence of being held to account and the absence of punishment.

In this noble verse there are benefits:

* The first benefit: the demonstration of Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, to hold the heavens and the earth. These great bodies Allah holds by His power without toil and without fatigue; He says to a thing "Be," and it is. ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38]. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly." They said, "We come willingly"﴾ [Fussilat 11].

* Among its benefits also: the demonstration of Allah's mercy, Mighty and Majestic, upon His servants, in that He subjected the heavens and the earth to them, and indeed subjected to them what is in the heavens and the earth as well, and this is from the perfection of His mercy. Were it not for Allah's mercy upon His servants, the heavens would fall upon the earth, people would perish, and not a creature would be left upon it.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that the heavens and the earth are created beings, among the totality of creatures, subjected by the command of Allah. This refutes the philosophers who say that the world is eternal and the spheres are eternal, and that the ninth sphere, as they claim, is the governor of what is beneath it. Rather, we say: all these spheres are created by Allah and subjected by His command; if Allah, Mighty and Majestic, willed them to cease, they would cease, and no one could hold them.

* A student: What is the point of this benefit?

* The Shaykh: The point is that they are created creatures of Allah, and therefore not eternal.

* A student: From where do we take it from the verse?

* The Shaykh: ﴿He holds the heavens﴾; their being held is evidence that they are standing by His command.

* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: that no one can govern these great, immense creatures; this is from His saying: ﴿And if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him.﴾

* Also among the benefits of this noble verse: the guidance of creation, that when they see in these signs in the heavens and the earth something that frightens and disturbs them, they should not turn to anyone except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Earthquakes, volcanoes, eclipses, thunderbolts and other things that terrify the world, we do not turn to in these matters except to Allah, for He is the one who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease, and no one holds them if they cease except Allah. But how do we turn to Allah in these matters? Do we turn to Him in the manner the Prophet, peace be upon him, guided us to in the eclipse prayer, or do we turn to Allah, Exalted, by general supplication, in the manner guided to by the Prophet ﷺ only in eclipses, and for anything else by general supplication? This is a matter of disagreement among the scholars. Some of them said: when frightening signs appear in the horizon that terrify the servants, it is legislated for the servants to pray the eclipse prayer until what is upon them is removed.

Those who said the first view, that one prays for every sign that frightens the servants, used as evidence the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed, the sun and the moon (...) Allah makes His servants afraid by them. So when you see them, that is, eclipsed, then pray and supplicate."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1048) from the hadith of Abu Bakrah.]] And so on to the end.

They said: the frightening of servants by thunderbolts and earthquakes has a stronger effect on their souls than an eclipse; so if the prayer is legislated for an eclipse, its legislation for these signs is all the more so. This is the view chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, and he cited the action of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he prayed the eclipse prayer during an earthquake.[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musannaf (8410) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] But the school (the Hanbalis) say that the eclipse prayer is only performed for an eclipse, or for an earthquake, relying on the action of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. However, the correct view is what Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah chose, for what he went to is indicated by the reason stated in the hadith: "Two of the signs of Allah, with which Allah makes His servants afraid."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (1048) from the hadith of Abu Bakrah.]]

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: establishing causation and reason in the actions of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; from His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [Fatir 41]. Establishing reasons in the acts of Allah or in His rulings indicates His perfection, not His deficiency, contrary to the deficient ones who claimed that establishing wisdom in the acts and rulings of Allah indicates deficiency; therefore they negated wisdom from the acts and rulings of Allah, saying: because that implies deficiency, and that He acts for a purpose, or rules for a purpose, and whoever acts for a purpose is deficient without it. On this basis, negating wisdom from the acts and rulings of Allah is said to be part of exalting Allah above deficiency.

In reality, any person who believes that establishing wisdom in the acts and rulings of Allah is a deficiency is himself the deficient one. Indeed, as soon as a person reflects on the matter he knows that whoever acts without wisdom has acted foolishly, and whoever acts with wisdom has acted rightly; for the wise person is the one who does a thing for a wise purpose and good disposition, while the foolish is the opposite. Therefore Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾ [an-Nisa 5]. On this basis, in this verse and in many other texts of the Book, the Sunnah and sound reason, there is evidence establishing wisdom for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that wisdom is among the most excellent attributes of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and explaining it in the rulings and acts of Allah is among the greatest and most evident matters.

We say: in the verse there is the establishment of wisdom, since He gave as the reason for holding the heavens and the earth what? That it is the requirement of His forbearance and forgiveness.

* Also among the benefits of the verse: the establishment of these two names for Allah, namely al-Halim and al-Ghafur, and the establishment of the attribute that they contain; for every name of Allah contains an attribute. There is no name of Allah that is purely a rigid noun at all, not even the name of majesty, Allah, which is not rigid but derived from divinity (al-uluhiyyah). Likewise the rest of the names are all not rigid but derived from meanings that indicate them, and the meanings indicated by Allah's names may be multiple in one name, as has passed concerning their indication, that they are indication by correspondence (mutabaqah), indication by inclusion (tadammun), and indication by implication (iltizam).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 42–43 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42]. ﴿And they swore﴾: the author said: i.e., (the disbelievers of Makkah). This allows for what he (may Allah have mercy on him) said, that the pronoun refers to the disbelievers of Makkah, and it also allows that it is more general, and that among the people there were those who swore who were not disbelievers of Makkah.

And His saying ﴿they swore by Allah﴾ means: they took oaths by Him.

And His saying ﴿their most emphatic oaths﴾ means: the utmost of oaths, i.e., the oaths in which they exerted their full effort, and these are oaths emphasized in their form, in quantity and in manner. Oaths emphasized in their form, in quantity and in manner are the oaths that reach the utmost effort, i.e., the greatest capacity of the one swearing. Oaths, as the scholars said, are emphasized in five respects: quantity, manner, time, place, and posture. Quantity is like saying: "By Allah, than whom there is no god but Him, the Mighty, the Dominant," and what is similar to that of the names that indicate retribution should the person be lying. This is emphasis by what? By quantity.

Emphasis by manner is by uttering it with intense emotion that shows his being moved by the oath. As for time, it is after the 'Asr prayer, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You shall detain the two after the prayer, and they will swear by Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah 106], so after the 'Asr prayer.

As for place, it is that the oath be made in a virtuous place, and the most virtuous places in the lands are the mosques. They said: it is at the mihrab or the pulpit in the congregational mosques, and at the Ka'bah. Some of them said: under the spout (al-Mizab), and in the Rawdah in Madinah. This is the matter of place.

As for posture, it is that one stands, because one is made to swear while standing. The scholars said: because punishment is closer to the one standing than to the one sitting. So these are five things in the emphasis of an oath. But did these disbelievers swear their most emphatic oaths with these five emphases? Allah knows best. In any case, they exerted the utmost of what they could in oaths.

﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42]. We say concerning the grammatical analysis of this sentence what we said concerning the first sentence, ﴿And if they were to cease, none could hold them back after Him﴾ [Fatir 41]. Here a conditional and an oath have come together, and the answer of the condition has been omitted; for this reason the lam appears in the answer, ﴿la-yakununna﴾ (they would surely be). If the omitted element were the answer of the oath, the lam would not have come in the answer, because the answer of the condition does not require the lam; rather it is connected by the fa' in its place, and it does not require a connecting element if it is not among the seven well-known positions.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿If a warner came to them﴾ [Fatir 42], meaning a warner, namely the Messenger ﴿they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42].

His saying ﴿la-yakununna﴾ with a damma on the nun is problematic: how was the nun given a damma? The known rule is that the imperfect verb with the emphatic nun is built on fathah, as in His saying: ﴿He will surely be thrown into the Crushing﴾ [al-Humazah 4]. Here He said ﴿la-yakununna﴾?

The answer to that is that the emphatic nun builds the verb with it only when it is directly attached to it, verbally and in estimation, and the nun here is directly attached to the verb verbally but not directly attached to it in estimation. How so? Because the verb here is for a group, not for a single person. Its original form is (yakunūnanna), and the nun was deleted to avoid the repetition of similar sounds, because they say that the Arabs dislike that three words of one type come together one after another, so they delete the first of them by elision; and the first to be deleted, according to their analogy, is the nun of the nominative, because its deletion is common, and because the emphatic nun came for a meaning which would be lost if it were deleted. When it comes for emphasis we do not delete it, but we delete the nun of the nominative, because its deletion is common.

We deleted the nun of the nominative, which is the first of the three. We said: la-yakūnūna; the waw remained following the nun, and the nun in this construction is a doubled letter, and a doubled letter begins with a sukun, does it not? It begins with a sukun. So we deleted the waw to avoid the meeting of two sukuns, and it became ﴿la-yakununna ahdā min iḥdā al-umam﴾. We deleted the waw between the verb's nuns; the nun in ﴿la-yakununna﴾ which is with us now is the nun of the verb, and for this reason we did not delete it, because it is original; we deleted the waw to avoid the meeting of two sukuns.

If someone says: we now have three nuns, and you have not deleted any one of them?

We say: first, these nuns are not connected in estimation; that is, some of them are not connected to the others in terms of estimation, because the waw that we deleted to avoid the meeting of two sukuns separates them.

Second, the nun that comes after the waw in ﴿la-yakununna﴾, the nun that is present now, is the nun of the verb, so it is part of the word's structure and cannot be deleted.

In any case, we must know the difference between (layakūnanna) and ﴿la-yakūnūna﴾ in the Qur'an: ﴿la-yakūnan﴾ ﴿He will surely be imprisoned and he will surely be among the humiliated﴾ [Yusuf 32]. So there is a difference between ﴿la-yakūnan﴾ and ﴿la-yakununna﴾. (Yakūnanna) is for the singular, and for this reason the verb is built on fathah with it, because it is connected to the emphatic nun verbally and in estimation; and ﴿la-yakununna﴾ is for the plural, and for this reason the verb is not built with it, because the emphatic nun does not directly attach to it in estimation. Is it clear? Or is there still a difficulty?

* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know! After all this long discussion, do we not understand?!
* Students: Clear.
* The Shaykh: Good. So the emphatic nun builds the verb with it only when it is directly attached to it, verbally and in estimation. In this sentence ﴿la-yakununna﴾, has it not attached to it in estimation, or verbally? In estimation. As for verbally, it has attached to it; we only said it did not attach to it in estimation because the waw of the plural was deleted from it, so it did not attach to it in estimation.

His saying ﴿aḥdā min iḥdā al-umam﴾ [Fatir 42]: ﴿aḥdā﴾ is the predicate of (yakūnu), so it is in the accusative with a fathah estimated on the alif, prevented from being apparent by the difficulty of pronunciation; and it is a comparative noun (ism al-tafḍīl).

His saying ﴿min iḥdā al-umam﴾: the author said: (the Jews and the Christians and others), i.e., any one of them, because of what they saw of some of them denying others; for the Jews said: the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians said: the Jews are not on anything. He says: ﴿they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾. They used ﴿iḥdā﴾, which indicates indefiniteness; they did not say: "better guided than the Christians," nor "better guided than the Jews." He said: ﴿min iḥdā al-umam﴾. Why? Because the matter was confusing to them: the Jews say the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians say the Jews are not on anything. And these polytheists, the disbelievers of Makkah, are an ignorant nation who do not know which side has the truth, so they did not say "better guided than the Christians," nor "better guided than the Jews," but said "better guided than one of them," i.e., better than any one of them, because the matter was confused for them. But the question remains: what is the evidence for restricting the word "nations" to the two nations, the Jewish and the Christian? And why should it not be said that it is more general than the Jews and the Christians? Because there are Magians who worship fire, and there may be other people who follow other religions. So for this we say: the answer is either that we hold to the generality and say: they say "better guided than any of the nations," i.e., of whatever nation it may be, such as the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, the idolaters who believe they are upon a religion, or what is similar to that, as if they were saying: better guided than all the nations, but they did not specify, because they did not know who was upon the truth. Or it is said: this plural is restricted to just two nations, because the known people who are upon a religion are who? The Jews and the Christians (...).

This is the correct view, but the end of his speech indicates that he meant only the Jews and the Christians: the truth became confused for them, so the Jews said: the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians said: the Jews are not on anything (...)

* * *

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ (...)

﴿there came to them a warner﴾ [Fatir 42].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But when there came to them a warner, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir 42]. Here Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿When there came to them a warner﴾ [Fatir 42], and did not say: "When the Messenger came to them," so that it would match what they said, to be more forceful in holding them to what they said; for they said: ﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely...﴾. When a warner came to them as they had stipulated and estimated, the matter came exactly so: ﴿When there came to them a warner﴾, as they themselves say, and it refers without doubt to Muhammad ﷺ, but as I pointed out, it was made indefinite and not definite, in following their speech, since they said: "A warner has come to us"; i.e., when a warner came to them exactly as they requested, in the very words, ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾. (Lamma) here is conditional, and its verb is ﴿came to them﴾ and its answer is ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾.

And (lamma) comes in the Arabic language in several ways:
One of them: as here, conditional.
The second: that it comes as a jussive particle like (lam), except that there are differences between them which is not the place to mention, since we have not spoken on grammar, as in His saying: ﴿Nay, but they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ [Sad 8], i.e., they have not tasted My punishment, but they are about to taste it.
The third: that it means (illa), as in His saying: ﴿There is no soul but that over it there is a guardian﴾ [al-Tariq 4], i.e., except that over it there is a guardian.
The fourth: that it means (ḥīn), bare of the conditional, as when you say: "I visited you when the dawn rose," i.e., at the time the dawn rose. These are four meanings of (lamma); here it is conditional: ﴿But when there came to them a warner, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir 42].

﴿It increased them﴾: the author said: (their coming), meaning that a warner came to them as they requested, but they were not more guided than any of the nations; rather it increased them in nothing but aversion from the truth and distance from following it. He said: (distance from guidance), and we seek refuge with Allah. This is a matter that is observed, for when the Prophet ﷺ was sent to the Quraysh, they turned away from him and harmed him by word and deed, and branded him with every defect, whereas before he was sent they held him in high regard, respected him, and called him "the Trustworthy." When he was sent, he was no longer trustworthy to them, and it was as if he were a different man from the one they knew. All of this refutes their saying: ﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42].

He said: (﴿in arrogance in the land﴾ [Fatir 43] away from faith, object of purpose). This means that the word ﴿arrogance﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu); i.e., it is accusative as an object of purpose: it increased them in nothing but aversion because of arrogance in the land. This is one of the two possibilities in the noble verse. The second possibility is that ﴿arrogance﴾ is a substitute for ﴿aversion﴾, i.e., it increased them in nothing but aversion, and this aversion is arrogance in the land, and this is a very strong possibility: that ﴿arrogance﴾ is a substitute or an explanatory apposition for ﴿aversion﴾. So this coming increased them in nothing but distance from the truth and arrogance in the land.

He said: ﴿and the evil plotting﴾ [Fatir 43], conjoined to ﴿arrogance﴾.

And ﴿plotting﴾: the author said: (the deed ﴿of evil﴾, from shirk and other things). He estimated the deed before ﴿evil﴾, so that evil is described as an attribute of the deed, and an evil deed is a plot. This is what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, held, so he made ﴿plotting﴾ annexed to a deleted noun, which is (the deed), and made ﴿evil﴾ an adjective of that deleted noun; i.e., the plotting of the evil deed; that is, they increased them in nothing but aversion and arrogance in the land, and that they plotted the plot of the evil deed. Plotting is deception, and it is reaching one's aim by hidden means to bring down one's adversary. This is plotting: that you reach, by hidden means, to bring down your opponent and enemy; as for reaching by apparent means, that is not plotting. If you say: this meaning does not apply to the deeds of these people, because these people display their evil deeds?

The answer: these people sometimes display it and sometimes conceal it, as in their gathering at the Dar al-Nadwah: what did they plan against the Messenger ﷺ? ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you or kill you or expel you, they plotted, and Allah plotted; and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30]. He mentioned plotting rather than the open, apparent matter, because it is more heinous than the open, apparent matter. So these people combined lying with plotting and deception, and we seek refuge with Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And the evil plot does not encompass﴾ — it encompasses ﴿the evil plot except its people﴾, and he is the plotter) and so on; i.e., these people plotted evil and did evil both openly and secretly. Does the one who plots against others escape? The answer: if it is an evil plot, then he does not escape, but his plot will encompass him and destroy him and annihilate him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there surrounded them that which they used to mock﴾ [Hud 8]. As for when the plotting is in the right, it does not encompass its people, but encompasses its enemy and does not encompass its doer; for plotting in the right is praiseworthy and not blameworthy.

He said: ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾. Here He did not say "except the plotter," but said "except its people," an indication of establishing the entitlement to this crime that was committed by him, and that he is worthy of having his plot encompass him. So every plotter without right is worthy that his plot encompass him.

He said: (The description of plotting as evil is the origin, and its annexation to it is before another usage in which an adjective was estimated, out of caution against annexation to an attribute.) This is a statement of little benefit and complicated meaning in reality.

He said: (The description of plotting as evil is the origin.) Where is the plotting? ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass﴾. The author says: (is the origin), meaning it follows the original form; for the original form is that the attribute is separate from the qualified noun and the qualified noun is not annexed to it. This is the origin. Pay attention! You say: "I passed by Zayd the excellent," making the attribute separate from the qualified noun, following it, not annexed to it.

So the author's saying (is the origin) means it is in accordance with the original form, since the original is that the attribute follows the qualified noun, not that the qualified noun is annexed to it. Do you now understand? This needs to be explained, because later the author's speech will be confusing to you; it came with "the origin."

(And its annexation to it is before another usage), (its annexation to it before), because in the sentence before this he said: ﴿and the plotting of the evil﴾, so here the plotting was not described as evil, but the plotting was annexed to the evil. So the author's saying, may Allah have mercy on him: (its annexation to it before) — what does (before) mean? It means before this sentence, and by it he means His saying: ﴿and the plotting of the evil﴾. (Another usage) — (before another usage) — is that in accordance with the origin or contrary to the origin? Contrary to the origin, because the original is that the attribute comes as a follower of the qualified noun, not that the qualified noun is annexed to the attribute. But it is permissible for the qualified noun to be annexed to its attribute; for this reason you constantly encounter the saying of the scholars: "This is from the category of annexing the qualified noun to its attribute," such as their saying: "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'); the original is "this is the congregational mosque," but it was annexed to its attribute. This is frequent. Similarly the attribute is sometimes annexed to the qualified noun, such as: "good of heart" (ṭāhir al-qalb); this is an attribute annexed to what it qualifies. As Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya:

"Like ṭāhir al-qalb, jamīl al-ẓāhir ∗∗∗ ........................"

This is from the category of annexing the attribute to the qualified noun. So from here we take that it is permissible to annex the attribute to the qualified noun and to annex the qualified noun to its attribute. What is the origin of that? The origin is that the attribute comes as a follower of the qualified noun, as a descriptor of it, and takes its case-ending. In the noble verse, is there annexation of the qualified noun to the attribute and description of the qualified noun by the attribute, or not? In the noble verse there is annexation of the qualified noun to the attribute and description of the qualified noun by the attribute, correct? In the verse, it is not a single word of them.

* A student: At its beginning and its end.

The Sheikh: In its beginning and its end, where is the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier?

A student: The second one (...).

The Sheikh: It is not the second, boy!

Students: The first, ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ ("and the evil scheming").

The Sheikh: The first: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. This is from the category of annexing the qualified noun to the qualifier (idafat al-mawsuf ila al-sifah). If it were outside the Qur'an and we wanted to convert it so that the adjective follows the noun, we would say: "arrogance on the earth and the evil scheming such-and-such," right? But here it has become an annexation: "and the scheming of the evil one."

And in it also is the description of the qualified noun by the qualifier. His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ﴾ ("And the evil scheming does not encompass anyone"). Which of them is the original? Here the author explained, saying: "Describing the scheming as evil is the original." It would have been clearer if he had said, instead of "original," "in accordance with the original," and this is what he means.

He said: "And its annexation to it is earlier." What does he mean by this? "Its annexation to it is earlier," meaning the annexation of the qualified noun to the qualifier. What does he mean by it from the verse? His saying: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾.

He says: "It is another usage," meaning it follows another usage in the Arabic language, because the Arabic language sometimes annexes the qualified noun to its qualifier. It is clear, I think?

He said: "A noun was assumed in it (qudira fihi mudaf)." According to his explanation and his tafsir, where he said: "﴿وَمَكْرَ﴾ the action ﴿السَّيِّئِ﴾."

He says: "Out of caution regarding annexation to the qualifier." What the last one said is disputed, because there is no need for that. There is no necessity to assume an omitted word in order to prevent the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier, because the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier is common and widespread in the Arabic language. This is not a matter to be avoided in Arabic, so that we would say we need to assume something to correct it. For this reason we say: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ is in accordance with its original form, meaning there is no need to assume anything omitted in it.

Then the Exalted said: (﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ "do they await?" ينتظرون), this is an explanation of (ينظرون) meaning "they await." There is a rule, though not a universal one, that (ينظر) if it is followed by (إلى) it means looking with the eye: ﴿أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ﴾ ("Then do they not look at the camels, how they were created?") [al-Ghashiyah 17]. If it is followed by (في) it means reflective contemplation, as in His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ ("Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth?") [al-A'raf 185]. If it is followed directly by its object, it means waiting, as here: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("Do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?") [Fatir 43]. Its meaning is: do they await, from waiting, which is expectation.

﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ means: they await, meaning they anticipate. ﴿إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: ﴿سُنَّتَ﴾ means the way or custom, and the annexation here to ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is an annexation of specification: meaning, except the custom that befell the former peoples. It does not mean the custom that the former peoples practiced, because ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ are those upon whom it was done, not those who did it. The doer is who? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: the author said: (Allah's custom regarding them, of punishing them for their denial of their messengers). Meaning: these who denied the Messenger ﷺ await nothing but the custom of the former peoples, and it, that is the custom of the former peoples, is punishment for their denial of the messengers.

He said: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ ("You will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any diversion in the way of Allah") [Fatir 43]: you will not find a change in the way of Allah by lifting it, or a transfer of it by altering it to other people. Meaning: the custom of Allah will fall upon the very persons who deserve it, so it will not be changed and removed, nor will it be transferred to other people, so that those who deserved it escape it. Rather, it befalls those who deserve it, specifically. An example: the polytheists who denied the Messenger ﷺ were from Quraysh. Transfer means that their punishment is transferred to the Banu Tamim, for example. Is this possible or not? It is not possible, because it is injustice for a people to be held accountable for the crime of others. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾. Quraysh denied the Messenger ﷺ, so instead of Allah punishing them, He bestowed blessings upon them. Is this possible or not?

Students: No.

The Sheikh: This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا﴾. So the punishment will not be changed into blessing, and it will not be transferred from its deserving recipient to other people. The custom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, must befall those who deserve it, without it being changed into a blessing, and without it being transferred to others. Why? Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is perfect in wisdom and perfect in justice. Perfect in wisdom, so He will not change vengeance into blessing for those who deserve it. Second, perfect in justice: He cannot transfer retribution to other people who do not deserve it. This attribute, ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا﴾ and so on, is from the category of negative attributes, but it includes the perfection of Allah's justice and the perfection of His wisdom. We may also say: and the completeness of His authority, such that no one can compel Him to transfer vengeance to others or to change it into blessing.

The author said: (That is, He does not replace the punishment with other than it, and it is not transferred, meaning the punishment, to other than its deserving recipient).

We take the benefits of the verses after His saying: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ ("And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths") [Fatir 42] and so on. Several benefits are derived from the two noble verses:

* Among them: when a person is in good health, or before the matter befalls him, he may find in himself the strength to carry it out. But when the matter befalls him, his condition changes. The indication: these people swore by Allah that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the (previous) nations. When the warner came to them, their condition changed. This frequently happens to humans: as long as a person has not been struck by the matter, he thinks he is capable of it, but when the matter strikes him, he is unable to bear it. For this reason, a person should not rush to judge himself by the condition in which he was safe from the matter befalling him, but should wait until the matter befalls him. Many people, for example, say: "I can endure the Hajj, and I will perform it," but when the time comes, they find the opposite in themselves. They say: "I can stand in prayer for the whole last third of the night," but when the matter becomes serious, they find themselves unable. The point is that a person should not be hasty, measuring his state in times of ease by his state when the matter befalls him, because man is a human being whose condition varies between being safe from the matter and the matter befalling him. And Allah knows best.

﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ and so on.

* In it are the two benefits you have heard: that when a person is in good health and free from the matter, he should not hasten, and should not measure himself in the time of trial by his state of ease, because a person may change.

* And in it also: evidence of the obstinacy of these people who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since before he was sent to them they swore the strongest oaths that they would be better guided than others, but when the Messenger ﷺ came to them, his coming increased them only in aversion.

And in it is an indication that a person should not make a vow, meaning to vow to perform an act of obedience, because he may not be granted success in fulfilling it. These people swore, and when the reason for obedience existed, they did not perform obedience to Allah. This is similar to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ قُلْ لَا تُقْسِمُوا طَاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ﴾ ("And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if you commanded them, they would go out. Say: Do not swear; obedience is known") [al-Nur 53]. They swore by Allah that if the Messenger ﷺ commanded them, they would go out, so Allah forbade them, and commanded His Prophet to say to them: "Do not swear." Similar to this is His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عَاهَدَ اللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٧٥) فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ﴾ ("And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous. But when He gave them of His bounty, they became miserly with it") [al-Tawbah 75-76]. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ forbade vowing, and explained that it brings no good.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: these people rejected the truth out of arrogance on the earth, meaning they desired arrogance. This is according to its grammatical analysis as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlih), meaning they only rejected the truth in order to have pride and exaltation on the earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: calling the actions of the disbelievers "scheming," based on His saying: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. We have mentioned in the tafsir that the actions of the disbelievers are divided into two types: one type in which they openly declare their disbelief, and they do not do it by way of scheming; and another type in which they do it by way of scheming. Which is worse? The second is worse. For this reason, no people schemed against their prophets except that Allah schemed against them, and the last of them was Muhammad ﷺ, when the people gathered in the Dar al-Nadwa to consult about what to do with him, so Allah schemed against them, glorified and exalted is He.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever intends evil, evil befalls him, based on His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ ("And the evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people"). Among the general maxims they say: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it." So when a person intends scheming, may Allah protect us, his scheme encompasses him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that scheming can be evil and can be good, based on His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾, and His saying before it: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. Indeed, Allah's scheming against His enemies who scheme against Him is good scheming, for which He is praised, and the scheming of those (...).

The one who causes the cause is awaiting the effect, whether he likes it or not. So we say to the sinful person: you are now awaiting punishment, anticipating it, even if it does not occur to his mind that he will be punished, because the doer of a cause awaits its effect, without fail.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the establishment of analogy (qiyas), or if you wish, say: the use of analogy, based on His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("Do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?") [Fatir 43], so he compares the condition of these people with the condition of the former peoples who denied and were punished.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the custom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding His servants is one: whoever obeys Allah, He rewards him, and whoever disobeys Allah, He punishes him, based on His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ ("You will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any diversion in the way of Allah") [Fatir 43]. It should not be said, for example: "We are a nation that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has honored, exalted and dignified, so He will not punish us as He punished those before us." Rather, we say: the requirement of honor is that we be more devoted in worship to Him than those who came before us, because when a person is honored, he should act in accordance with that honor. The mistreatment by one who did not honor you is not like the mistreatment by one who honored you (...) what is not obligatory upon anyone else.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of the power and wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since His custom is not changed or altered: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾.

The reason it is part of the perfection of power is that the powerless cannot make his actions follow a single pattern; rather they may be inconsistent and change due to his inability to maintain regularity. As for it being part of the perfection of wisdom, it is because the punishment of the earlier peoples was for a cause, and when this cause exists among later peoples, it takes its effect, because the requirement of wisdom is that causes are not separated from their effects. Thus in His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ there is an affirmation of the perfection of power and the perfection of wisdom.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that what continues and is adopted as a practice is called a sunnah. It is said: "This is so-and-so's sunnah," meaning his way. For this reason a distinction is made between the sunnah and the occasional act. An occasional act is one thing, and it cannot be made a regular practice, while what is consistently done is called a sunnah. This distinction is shown by the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Pray before the Maghrib, pray before the Maghrib." Then he said the third time: "For whoever wishes, lest people take it as a sunnah"[[Reported by al-Bukhari (1183) from the hadith of Abdullah al-Muzani.]]. Meaning: a consistent practice that they do continually.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 42–43 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42]. ﴿And they swore﴾: the author said: i.e., (the disbelievers of Makkah). This allows for what he (may Allah have mercy on him) said, that the pronoun refers to the disbelievers of Makkah, and it also allows that it is more general, and that among the people there were those who swore who were not disbelievers of Makkah.

And His saying ﴿they swore by Allah﴾ means: they took oaths by Him.

And His saying ﴿their most emphatic oaths﴾ means: the utmost of oaths, i.e., the oaths in which they exerted their full effort, and these are oaths emphasized in their form, in quantity and in manner. Oaths emphasized in their form, in quantity and in manner are the oaths that reach the utmost effort, i.e., the greatest capacity of the one swearing. Oaths, as the scholars said, are emphasized in five respects: quantity, manner, time, place, and posture. Quantity is like saying: "By Allah, than whom there is no god but Him, the Mighty, the Dominant," and what is similar to that of the names that indicate retribution should the person be lying. This is emphasis by what? By quantity.

Emphasis by manner is by uttering it with intense emotion that shows his being moved by the oath. As for time, it is after the 'Asr prayer, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You shall detain the two after the prayer, and they will swear by Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah 106], so after the 'Asr prayer.

As for place, it is that the oath be made in a virtuous place, and the most virtuous places in the lands are the mosques. They said: it is at the mihrab or the pulpit in the congregational mosques, and at the Ka'bah. Some of them said: under the spout (al-Mizab), and in the Rawdah in Madinah. This is the matter of place.

As for posture, it is that one stands, because one is made to swear while standing. The scholars said: because punishment is closer to the one standing than to the one sitting. So these are five things in the emphasis of an oath. But did these disbelievers swear their most emphatic oaths with these five emphases? Allah knows best. In any case, they exerted the utmost of what they could in oaths.

﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42]. We say concerning the grammatical analysis of this sentence what we said concerning the first sentence, ﴿And if they were to cease, none could hold them back after Him﴾ [Fatir 41]. Here a conditional and an oath have come together, and the answer of the condition has been omitted; for this reason the lam appears in the answer, ﴿la-yakununna﴾ (they would surely be). If the omitted element were the answer of the oath, the lam would not have come in the answer, because the answer of the condition does not require the lam; rather it is connected by the fa' in its place, and it does not require a connecting element if it is not among the seven well-known positions.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿If a warner came to them﴾ [Fatir 42], meaning a warner, namely the Messenger ﴿they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42].

His saying ﴿la-yakununna﴾ with a damma on the nun is problematic: how was the nun given a damma? The known rule is that the imperfect verb with the emphatic nun is built on fathah, as in His saying: ﴿He will surely be thrown into the Crushing﴾ [al-Humazah 4]. Here He said ﴿la-yakununna﴾?

The answer to that is that the emphatic nun builds the verb with it only when it is directly attached to it, verbally and in estimation, and the nun here is directly attached to the verb verbally but not directly attached to it in estimation. How so? Because the verb here is for a group, not for a single person. Its original form is (yakunūnanna), and the nun was deleted to avoid the repetition of similar sounds, because they say that the Arabs dislike that three words of one type come together one after another, so they delete the first of them by elision; and the first to be deleted, according to their analogy, is the nun of the nominative, because its deletion is common, and because the emphatic nun came for a meaning which would be lost if it were deleted. When it comes for emphasis we do not delete it, but we delete the nun of the nominative, because its deletion is common.

We deleted the nun of the nominative, which is the first of the three. We said: la-yakūnūna; the waw remained following the nun, and the nun in this construction is a doubled letter, and a doubled letter begins with a sukun, does it not? It begins with a sukun. So we deleted the waw to avoid the meeting of two sukuns, and it became ﴿la-yakununna ahdā min iḥdā al-umam﴾. We deleted the waw between the verb's nuns; the nun in ﴿la-yakununna﴾ which is with us now is the nun of the verb, and for this reason we did not delete it, because it is original; we deleted the waw to avoid the meeting of two sukuns.

If someone says: we now have three nuns, and you have not deleted any one of them?

We say: first, these nuns are not connected in estimation; that is, some of them are not connected to the others in terms of estimation, because the waw that we deleted to avoid the meeting of two sukuns separates them.

Second, the nun that comes after the waw in ﴿la-yakununna﴾, the nun that is present now, is the nun of the verb, so it is part of the word's structure and cannot be deleted.

In any case, we must know the difference between (layakūnanna) and ﴿la-yakūnūna﴾ in the Qur'an: ﴿la-yakūnan﴾ ﴿He will surely be imprisoned and he will surely be among the humiliated﴾ [Yusuf 32]. So there is a difference between ﴿la-yakūnan﴾ and ﴿la-yakununna﴾. (Yakūnanna) is for the singular, and for this reason the verb is built on fathah with it, because it is connected to the emphatic nun verbally and in estimation; and ﴿la-yakununna﴾ is for the plural, and for this reason the verb is not built with it, because the emphatic nun does not directly attach to it in estimation. Is it clear? Or is there still a difficulty?

* Students: (...).
* The Shaykh: By Allah, I do not know! After all this long discussion, do we not understand?!
* Students: Clear.
* The Shaykh: Good. So the emphatic nun builds the verb with it only when it is directly attached to it, verbally and in estimation. In this sentence ﴿la-yakununna﴾, has it not attached to it in estimation, or verbally? In estimation. As for verbally, it has attached to it; we only said it did not attach to it in estimation because the waw of the plural was deleted from it, so it did not attach to it in estimation.

His saying ﴿aḥdā min iḥdā al-umam﴾ [Fatir 42]: ﴿aḥdā﴾ is the predicate of (yakūnu), so it is in the accusative with a fathah estimated on the alif, prevented from being apparent by the difficulty of pronunciation; and it is a comparative noun (ism al-tafḍīl).

His saying ﴿min iḥdā al-umam﴾: the author said: (the Jews and the Christians and others), i.e., any one of them, because of what they saw of some of them denying others; for the Jews said: the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians said: the Jews are not on anything. He says: ﴿they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾. They used ﴿iḥdā﴾, which indicates indefiniteness; they did not say: "better guided than the Christians," nor "better guided than the Jews." He said: ﴿min iḥdā al-umam﴾. Why? Because the matter was confusing to them: the Jews say the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians say the Jews are not on anything. And these polytheists, the disbelievers of Makkah, are an ignorant nation who do not know which side has the truth, so they did not say "better guided than the Christians," nor "better guided than the Jews," but said "better guided than one of them," i.e., better than any one of them, because the matter was confused for them. But the question remains: what is the evidence for restricting the word "nations" to the two nations, the Jewish and the Christian? And why should it not be said that it is more general than the Jews and the Christians? Because there are Magians who worship fire, and there may be other people who follow other religions. So for this we say: the answer is either that we hold to the generality and say: they say "better guided than any of the nations," i.e., of whatever nation it may be, such as the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, the idolaters who believe they are upon a religion, or what is similar to that, as if they were saying: better guided than all the nations, but they did not specify, because they did not know who was upon the truth. Or it is said: this plural is restricted to just two nations, because the known people who are upon a religion are who? The Jews and the Christians (...).

This is the correct view, but the end of his speech indicates that he meant only the Jews and the Christians: the truth became confused for them, so the Jews said: the Christians are not on anything, and the Christians said: the Jews are not on anything (...)

* * *

I seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him﴾ (...)

﴿there came to them a warner﴾ [Fatir 42].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But when there came to them a warner, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir 42]. Here Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿When there came to them a warner﴾ [Fatir 42], and did not say: "When the Messenger came to them," so that it would match what they said, to be more forceful in holding them to what they said; for they said: ﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely...﴾. When a warner came to them as they had stipulated and estimated, the matter came exactly so: ﴿When there came to them a warner﴾, as they themselves say, and it refers without doubt to Muhammad ﷺ, but as I pointed out, it was made indefinite and not definite, in following their speech, since they said: "A warner has come to us"; i.e., when a warner came to them exactly as they requested, in the very words, ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾. (Lamma) here is conditional, and its verb is ﴿came to them﴾ and its answer is ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾.

And (lamma) comes in the Arabic language in several ways:
One of them: as here, conditional.
The second: that it comes as a jussive particle like (lam), except that there are differences between them which is not the place to mention, since we have not spoken on grammar, as in His saying: ﴿Nay, but they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ [Sad 8], i.e., they have not tasted My punishment, but they are about to taste it.
The third: that it means (illa), as in His saying: ﴿There is no soul but that over it there is a guardian﴾ [al-Tariq 4], i.e., except that over it there is a guardian.
The fourth: that it means (ḥīn), bare of the conditional, as when you say: "I visited you when the dawn rose," i.e., at the time the dawn rose. These are four meanings of (lamma); here it is conditional: ﴿But when there came to them a warner, it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾ [Fatir 42].

﴿It increased them﴾: the author said: (their coming), meaning that a warner came to them as they requested, but they were not more guided than any of the nations; rather it increased them in nothing but aversion from the truth and distance from following it. He said: (distance from guidance), and we seek refuge with Allah. This is a matter that is observed, for when the Prophet ﷺ was sent to the Quraysh, they turned away from him and harmed him by word and deed, and branded him with every defect, whereas before he was sent they held him in high regard, respected him, and called him "the Trustworthy." When he was sent, he was no longer trustworthy to them, and it was as if he were a different man from the one they knew. All of this refutes their saying: ﴿If a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [Fatir 42].

He said: (﴿in arrogance in the land﴾ [Fatir 43] away from faith, object of purpose). This means that the word ﴿arrogance﴾ is an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu); i.e., it is accusative as an object of purpose: it increased them in nothing but aversion because of arrogance in the land. This is one of the two possibilities in the noble verse. The second possibility is that ﴿arrogance﴾ is a substitute for ﴿aversion﴾, i.e., it increased them in nothing but aversion, and this aversion is arrogance in the land, and this is a very strong possibility: that ﴿arrogance﴾ is a substitute or an explanatory apposition for ﴿aversion﴾. So this coming increased them in nothing but distance from the truth and arrogance in the land.

He said: ﴿and the evil plotting﴾ [Fatir 43], conjoined to ﴿arrogance﴾.

And ﴿plotting﴾: the author said: (the deed ﴿of evil﴾, from shirk and other things). He estimated the deed before ﴿evil﴾, so that evil is described as an attribute of the deed, and an evil deed is a plot. This is what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, held, so he made ﴿plotting﴾ annexed to a deleted noun, which is (the deed), and made ﴿evil﴾ an adjective of that deleted noun; i.e., the plotting of the evil deed; that is, they increased them in nothing but aversion and arrogance in the land, and that they plotted the plot of the evil deed. Plotting is deception, and it is reaching one's aim by hidden means to bring down one's adversary. This is plotting: that you reach, by hidden means, to bring down your opponent and enemy; as for reaching by apparent means, that is not plotting. If you say: this meaning does not apply to the deeds of these people, because these people display their evil deeds?

The answer: these people sometimes display it and sometimes conceal it, as in their gathering at the Dar al-Nadwah: what did they plan against the Messenger ﷺ? ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you or kill you or expel you, they plotted, and Allah plotted; and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [al-Anfal 30]. He mentioned plotting rather than the open, apparent matter, because it is more heinous than the open, apparent matter. So these people combined lying with plotting and deception, and we seek refuge with Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And the evil plot does not encompass﴾ — it encompasses ﴿the evil plot except its people﴾, and he is the plotter) and so on; i.e., these people plotted evil and did evil both openly and secretly. Does the one who plots against others escape? The answer: if it is an evil plot, then he does not escape, but his plot will encompass him and destroy him and annihilate him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there surrounded them that which they used to mock﴾ [Hud 8]. As for when the plotting is in the right, it does not encompass its people, but encompasses its enemy and does not encompass its doer; for plotting in the right is praiseworthy and not blameworthy.

He said: ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass except its people﴾. Here He did not say "except the plotter," but said "except its people," an indication of establishing the entitlement to this crime that was committed by him, and that he is worthy of having his plot encompass him. So every plotter without right is worthy that his plot encompass him.

He said: (The description of plotting as evil is the origin, and its annexation to it is before another usage in which an adjective was estimated, out of caution against annexation to an attribute.) This is a statement of little benefit and complicated meaning in reality.

He said: (The description of plotting as evil is the origin.) Where is the plotting? ﴿And the evil plot does not encompass﴾. The author says: (is the origin), meaning it follows the original form; for the original form is that the attribute is separate from the qualified noun and the qualified noun is not annexed to it. This is the origin. Pay attention! You say: "I passed by Zayd the excellent," making the attribute separate from the qualified noun, following it, not annexed to it.

So the author's saying (is the origin) means it is in accordance with the original form, since the original is that the attribute follows the qualified noun, not that the qualified noun is annexed to it. Do you now understand? This needs to be explained, because later the author's speech will be confusing to you; it came with "the origin."

(And its annexation to it is before another usage), (its annexation to it before), because in the sentence before this he said: ﴿and the plotting of the evil﴾, so here the plotting was not described as evil, but the plotting was annexed to the evil. So the author's saying, may Allah have mercy on him: (its annexation to it before) — what does (before) mean? It means before this sentence, and by it he means His saying: ﴿and the plotting of the evil﴾. (Another usage) — (before another usage) — is that in accordance with the origin or contrary to the origin? Contrary to the origin, because the original is that the attribute comes as a follower of the qualified noun, not that the qualified noun is annexed to the attribute. But it is permissible for the qualified noun to be annexed to its attribute; for this reason you constantly encounter the saying of the scholars: "This is from the category of annexing the qualified noun to its attribute," such as their saying: "the mosque of the congregation" (masjid al-jami'); the original is "this is the congregational mosque," but it was annexed to its attribute. This is frequent. Similarly the attribute is sometimes annexed to the qualified noun, such as: "good of heart" (ṭāhir al-qalb); this is an attribute annexed to what it qualifies. As Ibn Malik said in the Alfiyya:

"Like ṭāhir al-qalb, jamīl al-ẓāhir ∗∗∗ ........................"

This is from the category of annexing the attribute to the qualified noun. So from here we take that it is permissible to annex the attribute to the qualified noun and to annex the qualified noun to its attribute. What is the origin of that? The origin is that the attribute comes as a follower of the qualified noun, as a descriptor of it, and takes its case-ending. In the noble verse, is there annexation of the qualified noun to the attribute and description of the qualified noun by the attribute, or not? In the noble verse there is annexation of the qualified noun to the attribute and description of the qualified noun by the attribute, correct? In the verse, it is not a single word of them.

* A student: At its beginning and its end.

The Sheikh: In its beginning and its end, where is the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier?

A student: The second one (...).

The Sheikh: It is not the second, boy!

Students: The first, ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ ("and the evil scheming").

The Sheikh: The first: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. This is from the category of annexing the qualified noun to the qualifier (idafat al-mawsuf ila al-sifah). If it were outside the Qur'an and we wanted to convert it so that the adjective follows the noun, we would say: "arrogance on the earth and the evil scheming such-and-such," right? But here it has become an annexation: "and the scheming of the evil one."

And in it also is the description of the qualified noun by the qualifier. His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ﴾ ("And the evil scheming does not encompass anyone"). Which of them is the original? Here the author explained, saying: "Describing the scheming as evil is the original." It would have been clearer if he had said, instead of "original," "in accordance with the original," and this is what he means.

He said: "And its annexation to it is earlier." What does he mean by this? "Its annexation to it is earlier," meaning the annexation of the qualified noun to the qualifier. What does he mean by it from the verse? His saying: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾.

He says: "It is another usage," meaning it follows another usage in the Arabic language, because the Arabic language sometimes annexes the qualified noun to its qualifier. It is clear, I think?

He said: "A noun was assumed in it (qudira fihi mudaf)." According to his explanation and his tafsir, where he said: "﴿وَمَكْرَ﴾ the action ﴿السَّيِّئِ﴾."

He says: "Out of caution regarding annexation to the qualifier." What the last one said is disputed, because there is no need for that. There is no necessity to assume an omitted word in order to prevent the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier, because the annexation of the qualified noun to its qualifier is common and widespread in the Arabic language. This is not a matter to be avoided in Arabic, so that we would say we need to assume something to correct it. For this reason we say: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾ is in accordance with its original form, meaning there is no need to assume anything omitted in it.

Then the Exalted said: (﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ "do they await?" ينتظرون), this is an explanation of (ينظرون) meaning "they await." There is a rule, though not a universal one, that (ينظر) if it is followed by (إلى) it means looking with the eye: ﴿أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ﴾ ("Then do they not look at the camels, how they were created?") [al-Ghashiyah 17]. If it is followed by (في) it means reflective contemplation, as in His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا فِي مَلَكُوتِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ ("Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth?") [al-A'raf 185]. If it is followed directly by its object, it means waiting, as here: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("Do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?") [Fatir 43]. Its meaning is: do they await, from waiting, which is expectation.

﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ means: they await, meaning they anticipate. ﴿إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: ﴿سُنَّتَ﴾ means the way or custom, and the annexation here to ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ is an annexation of specification: meaning, except the custom that befell the former peoples. It does not mean the custom that the former peoples practiced, because ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ are those upon whom it was done, not those who did it. The doer is who? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: the author said: (Allah's custom regarding them, of punishing them for their denial of their messengers). Meaning: these who denied the Messenger ﷺ await nothing but the custom of the former peoples, and it, that is the custom of the former peoples, is punishment for their denial of the messengers.

He said: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ ("You will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any diversion in the way of Allah") [Fatir 43]: you will not find a change in the way of Allah by lifting it, or a transfer of it by altering it to other people. Meaning: the custom of Allah will fall upon the very persons who deserve it, so it will not be changed and removed, nor will it be transferred to other people, so that those who deserved it escape it. Rather, it befalls those who deserve it, specifically. An example: the polytheists who denied the Messenger ﷺ were from Quraysh. Transfer means that their punishment is transferred to the Banu Tamim, for example. Is this possible or not? It is not possible, because it is injustice for a people to be held accountable for the crime of others. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾. Quraysh denied the Messenger ﷺ, so instead of Allah punishing them, He bestowed blessings upon them. Is this possible or not?

Students: No.

The Sheikh: This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا﴾. So the punishment will not be changed into blessing, and it will not be transferred from its deserving recipient to other people. The custom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, must befall those who deserve it, without it being changed into a blessing, and without it being transferred to others. Why? Because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is perfect in wisdom and perfect in justice. Perfect in wisdom, so He will not change vengeance into blessing for those who deserve it. Second, perfect in justice: He cannot transfer retribution to other people who do not deserve it. This attribute, ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا﴾ and so on, is from the category of negative attributes, but it includes the perfection of Allah's justice and the perfection of His wisdom. We may also say: and the completeness of His authority, such that no one can compel Him to transfer vengeance to others or to change it into blessing.

The author said: (That is, He does not replace the punishment with other than it, and it is not transferred, meaning the punishment, to other than its deserving recipient).

We take the benefits of the verses after His saying: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ ("And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths") [Fatir 42] and so on. Several benefits are derived from the two noble verses:

* Among them: when a person is in good health, or before the matter befalls him, he may find in himself the strength to carry it out. But when the matter befalls him, his condition changes. The indication: these people swore by Allah that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the (previous) nations. When the warner came to them, their condition changed. This frequently happens to humans: as long as a person has not been struck by the matter, he thinks he is capable of it, but when the matter strikes him, he is unable to bear it. For this reason, a person should not rush to judge himself by the condition in which he was safe from the matter befalling him, but should wait until the matter befalls him. Many people, for example, say: "I can endure the Hajj, and I will perform it," but when the time comes, they find the opposite in themselves. They say: "I can stand in prayer for the whole last third of the night," but when the matter becomes serious, they find themselves unable. The point is that a person should not be hasty, measuring his state in times of ease by his state when the matter befalls him, because man is a human being whose condition varies between being safe from the matter and the matter befalling him. And Allah knows best.

﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ and so on.

* In it are the two benefits you have heard: that when a person is in good health and free from the matter, he should not hasten, and should not measure himself in the time of trial by his state of ease, because a person may change.

* And in it also: evidence of the obstinacy of these people who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, since before he was sent to them they swore the strongest oaths that they would be better guided than others, but when the Messenger ﷺ came to them, his coming increased them only in aversion.

And in it is an indication that a person should not make a vow, meaning to vow to perform an act of obedience, because he may not be granted success in fulfilling it. These people swore, and when the reason for obedience existed, they did not perform obedience to Allah. This is similar to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ لَئِنْ أَمَرْتَهُمْ لَيَخْرُجُنَّ قُلْ لَا تُقْسِمُوا طَاعَةٌ مَعْرُوفَةٌ﴾ ("And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if you commanded them, they would go out. Say: Do not swear; obedience is known") [al-Nur 53]. They swore by Allah that if the Messenger ﷺ commanded them, they would go out, so Allah forbade them, and commanded His Prophet to say to them: "Do not swear." Similar to this is His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ عَاهَدَ اللَّهَ لَئِنْ آتَانَا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ وَلَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ (٧٥) فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ﴾ ("And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous. But when He gave them of His bounty, they became miserly with it") [al-Tawbah 75-76]. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ forbade vowing, and explained that it brings no good.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: these people rejected the truth out of arrogance on the earth, meaning they desired arrogance. This is according to its grammatical analysis as an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlih), meaning they only rejected the truth in order to have pride and exaltation on the earth.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: calling the actions of the disbelievers "scheming," based on His saying: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. We have mentioned in the tafsir that the actions of the disbelievers are divided into two types: one type in which they openly declare their disbelief, and they do not do it by way of scheming; and another type in which they do it by way of scheming. Which is worse? The second is worse. For this reason, no people schemed against their prophets except that Allah schemed against them, and the last of them was Muhammad ﷺ, when the people gathered in the Dar al-Nadwa to consult about what to do with him, so Allah schemed against them, glorified and exalted is He.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: whoever intends evil, evil befalls him, based on His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾ ("And the evil scheming does not encompass anyone except its own people"). Among the general maxims they say: "Whoever digs a pit for his brother falls into it." So when a person intends scheming, may Allah protect us, his scheme encompasses him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that scheming can be evil and can be good, based on His saying: ﴿وَلَا يَحِيقُ الْمَكْرُ السَّيِّئُ إِلَّا بِأَهْلِهِ﴾, and His saying before it: ﴿وَمَكْرَ السَّيِّئِ﴾. Indeed, Allah's scheming against His enemies who scheme against Him is good scheming, for which He is praised, and the scheming of those (...).

The one who causes the cause is awaiting the effect, whether he likes it or not. So we say to the sinful person: you are now awaiting punishment, anticipating it, even if it does not occur to his mind that he will be punished, because the doer of a cause awaits its effect, without fail.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the establishment of analogy (qiyas), or if you wish, say: the use of analogy, based on His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا سُنَّتَ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ ("Do they await anything but the way of the former peoples?") [Fatir 43], so he compares the condition of these people with the condition of the former peoples who denied and were punished.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the custom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, regarding His servants is one: whoever obeys Allah, He rewards him, and whoever disobeys Allah, He punishes him, based on His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ ("You will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any diversion in the way of Allah") [Fatir 43]. It should not be said, for example: "We are a nation that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has honored, exalted and dignified, so He will not punish us as He punished those before us." Rather, we say: the requirement of honor is that we be more devoted in worship to Him than those who came before us, because when a person is honored, he should act in accordance with that honor. The mistreatment by one who did not honor you is not like the mistreatment by one who honored you (...) what is not obligatory upon anyone else.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the perfection of the power and wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, since His custom is not changed or altered: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾.

The reason it is part of the perfection of power is that the powerless cannot make his actions follow a single pattern; rather they may be inconsistent and change due to his inability to maintain regularity. As for it being part of the perfection of wisdom, it is because the punishment of the earlier peoples was for a cause, and when this cause exists among later peoples, it takes its effect, because the requirement of wisdom is that causes are not separated from their effects. Thus in His saying: ﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا وَلَنْ تَجِدَ لِسُنَّتِ اللَّهِ تَحْوِيلًا﴾ there is an affirmation of the perfection of power and the perfection of wisdom.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that what continues and is adopted as a practice is called a sunnah. It is said: "This is so-and-so's sunnah," meaning his way. For this reason a distinction is made between the sunnah and the occasional act. An occasional act is one thing, and it cannot be made a regular practice, while what is consistently done is called a sunnah. This distinction is shown by the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Pray before the Maghrib, pray before the Maghrib." Then he said the third time: "For whoever wishes, lest people take it as a sunnah"[[Reported by al-Bukhari (1183) from the hadith of Abdullah al-Muzani.]]. Meaning: a consistent practice that they do continually.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 35, verse 44 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength?﴾ [Fatir 44]. The hamzah here is interrogative, and its purpose is reproach and rebuke. Is this interrogative hamzah attached to the sentence that is actually stated, or to an omitted sentence that the context determines?

On this, the grammarians have two opinions. Some of them say that it is attached to the sentence that is stated. According to this view, they say the underlying sense is: "And have they not travelled...", so they treat the waw as preceding the hamzah, since the hamzah cannot be considered to precede the waw. The waw is a conjunctive particle (harf 'atf) which requires something to be conjoined to, so they say the hamzah is placed later and the waw is a conjunction, and this sentence is conjoined to what came before. This approach is without doubt the easier and simpler one, since a person does not have to strain himself over an omitted, implied element. The second opinion is that the hamzah is attached to an omitted element that the context determines. In verses like this one, we say the sense of the sentence is: "Did they neglect, and not travel through the earth?" or a similar expression.

This estimate may be easy in some places, in the sense that in some places the meaning is apparent and you can easily supply that omitted element. But sometimes it is difficult for you to supply that omitted element, because the context permits several possibilities. In this case we say: is the second opinion or the first better? The second, in terms of what is generally the case. The other opinion is closer and easier, so we say that the other opinion is closer and easier: to make the waw a conjunction, and this sentence is conjoined to what came before. The original structure is to place that conjunctive particle before the sentence, so the sense is: "And have they not travelled..."

As for his saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth﴾, is the travelling here a travelling of the hearts, a travelling of the feet, or both? We say the better view is that it is comprehensive, so it includes the travelling of the hearts and the travelling of the feet. The travelling of the hearts is by considering the history of the earlier nations, what happened to them, and what happened to the people of goodness who commanded justice. A person travels in his heart throughout the regions of the world while sitting on his chair without moving. As for physical travel, or travel on foot, it is that a person goes to these places in order to take a lesson. From this is the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Visit the graves, for they remind you of the Hereafter" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3235), al-Tirmidhi (1054), and al-Nasa'i (5651) from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb.]].
